jobs.title: Senior Engineer - Technical Staff
jobs.description:
ABOUT SAVVY WEALTH:

Wealth management is a $545 billion industry that still runs on manual work. 75% of advisors offer no digital communication beyond email, and most still build financial plans by hand in Excel. Savvy is reinventing what it looks like to be a financial advisor. Founder Ritik Malhotra saw the fragmentation firsthand after seeking out his own advisor, and started Savvy to give independent advisors a modern, AI-native home.



Savvy is a registered investment advisor (RIA), and we partner with experienced financial advisors who want to grow without running the back office themselves. Advisors bring their book and join Savvy, running under their own brand (or ours), and Savvy earns a percentage of the assets they manage. In return, they get a true business-in-a-box: a proprietary tech platform and client portal, an in-house marketing team that helps them grow, a world-class investment management team, and a dedicated client services team that runs day-to-day operations and support. Advisors at Savvy service up to 50% more households and save 19 hours a week.



AI runs through everything we do. On the product side, Savvy Intelligence (released April 2026) is the only AI built for wealth managers that can see a client's complete financial picture. Internally, everyone at Savvy uses Claude and is encouraged to experiment with it, backed by a dedicated AI enablement team and a RevOps org building agents in-house.



The trajectory is steep and it's still early. We're a Series C company with 170+ people, $200M raised, and $100M ARR in sight this year. Inc. ranked us the No. 1 fastest-growing financial services company in America in 2026. Come build the next stage with us!



Recognition:

We're a Certified Great Place to Work and have been honored for our culture and our growth:

 - Newsweek's America's Greatest Startup Workplaces (2026)

 - Fortune Best Workplaces in New York™ (2026)

 - Great Place to Work Certified™ 
   
   

The role:

Savvy is hiring a Senior Engineer to lead the design and delivery of complex product and platform work. Our platform is where AI meets fiduciary advice, and the senior engineers who build it don't just use AI to go faster, they make decisions about where AI belongs in the system, how to build it reliably, and how to raise the team's ability to do the same. You'll own end-to-end delivery of high-impact projects, establish engineering patterns for the team, and help define how our platform evolves as we scale.


Responsibilities:

 - Lead the design and delivery of complex product features and platform systems, from scoping and architecture through production and iteration.

 - Apply and champion AI tooling (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and the rest) to accelerate your own output and raise the team's velocity.

 - Drive architectural decisions: data models, service boundaries, system tradeoffs, and communicate them clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

 - Mentor engineers, give substantive feedback, and be a go-to resource for technical judgment across the team.

 - Partner with Product and Design to shape scope and de-risk execution on high-ambiguity problems.

 - Work directly with our customers (financial advisors) to understand their workflows and bring that context into how you build.

Must have:

 - 5+ years of professional experience.

 - You use AI tools aggressively in your daily workflow: Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and whatever else is useful. You're consistently ahead of the curve on what's emerging, and you translate that into concrete decisions: what to build with AI, how to build it reliably, and where it's not worth the complexity.

 - Track record of leading projects end-to-end with measurable business impact; you've taken ambiguous problems from 0 to production and held the quality bar throughout.

 - Strong full-stack or platform engineering depth; we use Rails, React, Next.js, PostgreSQL, and GraphQL; comfortable across the stack or with the depth to close gaps fast.

 - Strong system design instincts: data models, service boundaries, failure modes, and how systems hold up at scale.

Nice to have:

jobs.title: Senior/Staff Manufacturing Engineer – Advanced Processes
jobs.description:
WHAT TO EXPECT

Heron Power is a startup company building cutting-edge power electronics for the 21st-century grid. We aim to debottleneck the growth of electricity generation and consumption with scalable, innovative, and less costly hardware solutions, accelerating the electrification of everything.

Our first goal is to build better converters (inverters & rectifiers) to connect large-scale renewables, storage, and loads to the grid. Heron’s leadership team is made up of seasoned veterans who have designed and shipped gigawatts of power conversion products over the past decade.

We understand that no one individual knows everything. We will all learn a lot together and from each other. We strive to build a collaborative, enriching environment conducive to personal, technical, and career growth. You can expect to work in a dynamic and collaborative environment, driven by first principles engineering, solving difficult problems.




JOB OVERVIEW

As a Sr./Staff Manufacturing Engineer - Advanced Processes, Inspection & Test, you will be responsible for developing, testing, deploying and scaling the processes, inline inspection and electrical test strategies that guarantee high process capability at line rate for our high-volume transformer assembly lines. This role spans medium to high viscosity potting and dispense systems, surface treatment, high-speed plastic welding – from void, surface energy and delamination detection to a variety of electrical tests. You will work closely with product, mechanical and electrical design teams early and often through DFM, design processes from a first principles approach and close the feedback loop to ensure both the product and the lines that make it are robust. You will collaborate closely with external suppliers and equipment partners to land scalable, reliable and highly repeatable equipment lines and processes, owning them from concept to production ramp.




HOW YOU WILL CONTRIBUTE

 - Lead development of inline inspection, process monitoring and automated electrical test across the Transformer Assembly line, from concept and vendor selection through FAT/SAT, commissioning, validation and ramp

 - Develop and deploy high-speed automated inspection of potted assemblies for voids, delamination, incomplete fill and cure defects – using technologies such as inline X-ray/CT, ultrasonic, thermography and machine vision

 - Develop surface treatments processes such as atmospheric plasma/corona treatment, solvent/chemical cleaning and adhesion preparation along with inline verification of treatment uniformity and quality (surface energy, contact angle etc)

 - Architect and deploy automated high volume electrical test equipment – capacitance, inductance, DC resistance, conductivity/resistivity, impulse, AC resistance, hipot and partial discharge – including test sequencing, fixturing, shielding/noise control, limit setting to balance cycle time, yield and escape risk

 - Partner with other manufacturing engineers in developing high-viscosity 1k/2k potting and dispense systems, high-speed plastic welding processes like ultrasonic, hot plate and IR welding with robust inline process monitoring and destructive/non-destructive weld validation

 - Lead MSA, Gage R&R and test method validation for inspection and electrical test systems, including golden/limit samples and correlation to lab methods such as sectioning and CT

 - Apply PFMEA, control plans, SPC methodology and structured problem solving to maintain world class process capability

 - Support automation integration with robots, conveyors and inline QA




WHAT YOU WILL BRING




MUST-HAVE REQUIREMENTS

We have a short list of must-have requirements. We prioritize a strong grip on first principles, hands-on skills, and a sense of initiative. Domain-specific knowledge and experience will help determine the career level for each hire.

 - Bachelor’s degree in Manufacturing/Industrial/Mechanical/Electrical/Chemical Engineering

 - 7+ years of experience in high volume manufacturing with a focus on process engineering, inline inspection, production test or automation for electromechanical, power electronics, magnetics or battery products

 - Hands-one experience deploying automated non-destructive inspection (X-ray/Ct, ultrasonic, thermography or vision) to detect voids, delamination or bond-line defects in production

 - Experience developing and validating automated electrical test for high volume production

 - Experience with design, optimization and validation for high-viscosity potting and dispense systems including material supply, metering, mixing, vacuum potting and degassing strategies

 - Experience with surface preparation processes and quantitative surface quality measurement

 - Experience with ultrasonic, hot plate and/or IR welding of plastics, including process monitoring and weld validation

 - Proficiency in statistical analysis, SPC, Cp/Cpk studies, hypothesis testing and Minitab/JMP

 - Demonstrated ability to run DoE’s and optimize complex processes

 - Experience implementing PFMEA’s, control plans, process flow diagrams

 - Hands-on experience with automation, robotics, PLCs and vision systems


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with injection molding processes and tooling

If you are passionate about technology and enjoy working in a fast-paced environment, we would love to hear from you. Join us in accelerating the electrification of everything at Heron Power.

Heron Power provides competitive compensation (salary and equity) and benefits. The salary for this role ranges from $130,000 to $180,000 per year.

jobs.title: Fleet Safety & Compliance Coordinator
jobs.description:
Fleet Safety & Compliance Coordinator - Savannah, GA

Location: Savannah, GA

Employment Type: Full-Time | On-Site (Monday-Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM with occasional weekends | Experienced

Compensation: $80,000 - $90,000 depending on experience and qualifications

This is not a remote position. Relocation assistance is not offered.

About the Role

Cargomatic is committed to making the lives of truckers and shippers easier. Our goal is to let truckers be truckers and shippers be shippers by simplifying the process for all our customers and vendors.

Cargomatic was named to the Built In Best Places to Work list, recognizing our people-first culture, strong benefits, and commitment to employee growth and well-being.

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced Fleet Safety & Compliance Coordinator to support a fleet of more than 100 trucks operating in port and rail drayage. This role will support driver onboarding, DOT and safety compliance, equipment registrations, fuel card administration, and day-to-day fleet administration.

The ideal candidate has strong, hands-on experience managing safety and compliance for a trucking company and understands the unique requirements of port and rail operations. This is an execution-focused role requiring someone who can manage multiple processes, maintain accurate records, resolve issues, and keep drivers and equipment compliant and operational.

Key Responsibilities

Safety & Regulatory Compliance

• Maintain driver and equipment compliance with applicable DOT and FMCSA requirements.

• Monitor Hours of Service (HOS), electronic logging devices (ELDs), and driver logs.

• Monitor driver activity and safety exceptions through Samsara and other fleet technology platforms.

• Maintain driver qualification files, licenses, medical certifications, and required safety documentation.

• Track compliance deadlines, renewals, violations, and corrective actions.

• Coordinate accident and incident reporting, documentation, and follow-up.

• Support internal audits and maintain organized, accurate compliance records.

Driver Onboarding

• Coordinate onboarding for new company drivers and owner-operators, ensuring all required documents and qualifications are completed before dispatch.

• Verify driver credentials, required registrations, insurance documents, and other onboarding requirements.

• Coordinate with recruiting, dispatch, operations, and other internal teams to resolve onboarding issues.

• Track onboarding progress and ensure drivers are approved and ready to operate.

Fleet Registration & IRP Administration

• Manage and coordinate the International Registration Plan (IRP) plate program, including applications, renewals, supporting documentation, and recordkeeping.

• Track registration and plate expiration dates to prevent interruptions to operations.

• Maintain accurate records for trucks, plates, permits, and related fleet documentation.

• Coordinate with state agencies and registration providers as needed.

Fuel Card Administration

• Coordinate fuel card setup, issuance, assignment, and cancellation for drivers.

• Maintain accurate fuel card records and support access or transaction-related issues.

• Assist with monitoring fuel card exceptions and escalating suspected misuse or discrepancies.

• Coordinate with Finance and Operations to ensure fuel cards are assigned appropriately and available when drivers are ready to work.

Systems & Operational Support

• Maintain accurate driver, truck, and compliance information across company systems.

• Use Samsara and other fleet management systems to monitor driver and equipment compliance.

• Support Trinium data maintenance and operational workflows as needed.

• Maintain accurate SCAC code and other carrier or customer-required information, as applicable.

• Work closely with Operations and Dispatch to ensure drivers and trucks meet the requirements for port, rail, and customer operations.

• Provide timely updates on outstanding compliance items that could prevent a driver or truck from being dispatched.

Qualifications

• Minimum 5 years of hands-on experience in fleet safety, DOT compliance, or trucking fleet administration required.

• Experience supporting a commercial trucking fleet, preferably 100+ trucks.

• Strong understanding of DOT/FMCSA regulations, Hours of Service, ELDs, and driver qualification requirements.

• Experience with Samsara or comparable fleet safety and telematics platforms.

• Working knowledge of IRP plates, registrations, permits, and renewal processes.

• Experience administering driver onboarding and fuel card programs.

• Understanding of port and rail drayage operations and related driver, equipment, and carrier requirements.

• Familiarity with SCAC codes and port/rail operating requirements.

• Trinium experience is a plus.

• Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.

• Ability to manage multiple deadlines, follow through on open issues, and work independently.

• Strong communication skills and the ability to coordinate across Safety, Recruiting, Dispatch, Operations, and Finance.

The Ideal Candidate

The successful candidate is a hands-on fleet safety and compliance professional who understands that compliance directly affects fleet availability and daily operations.

They are organized, proactive, detail-oriented, and comfortable managing the administrative requirements of a large trucking fleet. They identify problems before they interrupt operations, follow through on outstanding items, and work collaboratively to ensure drivers and equipment remain compliant and ready to operate.

Measures of Success

• Drivers are fully qualified and compliant before dispatch.

• DOT and safety records remain current and audit-ready.

• IRP plates, registrations, and renewals are completed on time.

• Fuel cards are issued, maintained, and deactivated accurately.

• Safety and compliance exceptions are identified and addressed promptly.

• Driver and truck information is accurate across company systems.

• Fleet availability is protected by preventing avoidable compliance and administrative delays.

Benefits & Perks
Cargomatic offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support our employees’ health, financial well-being, and work-life balance:

• Medical, dental, and vision insurance

• 401(k) with company match

• Paid time off (PTO) and company holidays

• Life and disability insurance

• Flexible work environment (where applicable)

• Career growth and advancement opportunities

• Employee recognition and wellness programs

Why Join Cargomatic?
At Cargomatic, you’ll have the opportunity to make a direct impact on how freight moves through critical supply chain networks. You’ll work with a fast-growing, technology-driven logistics company that values innovation, ownership, and operational excellence.

Equal Opportunity Employer
Cargomatic is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

jobs.title: Senior Client Associate (West Coast)
jobs.description:
ABOUT SAVVY WEALTH:

Wealth management is a $545 billion industry that still runs on manual work. 75% of advisors offer no digital communication beyond email, and most still build financial plans by hand in Excel. Savvy is reinventing what it looks like to be a financial advisor. Founder Ritik Malhotra saw the fragmentation firsthand after seeking out his own advisor, and started Savvy to give independent advisors a modern, AI-native home.



Savvy is a registered investment advisor (RIA), and we partner with experienced financial advisors who want to grow without running the back office themselves. Advisors bring their book and join Savvy, running under their own brand (or ours), and Savvy earns a percentage of the assets they manage. In return, they get a true business-in-a-box: a proprietary tech platform and client portal, an in-house marketing team that helps them grow, a world-class investment management team, and a dedicated client services team that runs day-to-day operations and support. Advisors at Savvy service up to 50% more households and save 19 hours a week.



AI runs through everything we do. On the product side, Savvy Intelligence (released April 2026) is the only AI built for wealth managers that can see a client's complete financial picture. Internally, everyone at Savvy uses Claude and is encouraged to experiment with it, backed by a dedicated AI enablement team and a RevOps org building agents in-house.



The trajectory is steep and it's still early. We're a Series C company with 170+ people, $200M raised, and $100M ARR in sight this year. Inc. ranked us the No. 1 fastest-growing financial services company in America in 2026. Come build the next stage with us!



Recognition:

We're a Certified Great Place to Work and have been honored for our culture and our growth:

 - Newsweek's America's Greatest Startup Workplaces (2026)

 - Fortune Best Workplaces in New York™ (2026)

 - Great Place to Work Certified™ 
   
   

The Role:
The Savvy team is looking for an experienced Senior Client Associate who is ready to apply  their exceptional client service skills to drive impact in a fast-paced and growing environment. In this role, you’ll serve as a dedicated operational partner to multiple advisors, ensuring their clients receive exceptional day-to-day support. The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, an  excellent problem-solver, and a strong communicator who can help foster long-term client  relationships. 



This role will be critical in shaping our standard operating procedures and  ensuring we set the highest standard for client and advisor support. As an early member of the  Savvy team, you will help build out the client servicing function. You will also work closely with  the Product and Operations teams to shape the future roadmap of Savvy's product and advisory services.



Responsibilities: 

 - Responsible for day-to-day operations and administrative support of Savvy wealth  managers, providing exceptional client service and fostering long-term client relationships.

 - Own best-in-class execution of all client tasks, requests and inquiries in a timely manner.

 - Proactively seek out opportunities to improve Savvy's internal procedures in pursuit of the best advisor and client experience.

 - Streamline new client prospecting, closing, and onboarding processes including meeting preparation, obtaining account and investment strategy documentation, and driving account creation and transfers.

 - Assist advisors by executing investment transactions and fulfilling account billing & performance reporting tasks.

 - Work closely with other professional advisors such as CPAs, estate planning attorneys, business managers, insurance agents, and more.

 - Create and maintain client data in Salesforce and other systems.

 - Ensure Savvy is adhering to all required compliance policies and procedures.

 - Protect clients by maintaining confidentiality of all personal and financial information.
   
   

Must Have:

 - 2+ years of experience in a similar role with a registered investment advisory firm and/or broker-dealer including experience interacting directly with clients AND advisors.

 - A high-energy, collaborative, and self-starter attitude; willing to roll up your sleeves and have an incredible ownership mentality.

 - Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.

 - Strong technical skills in Google Suite applications--Word, Excel, and Powerpoint-- and familiarity with the MS Office equivalents.

 - Detail-oriented and organized, with the ability to prioritize and juggle multiple tasks at once.

 - Adept at quickly learning and adopting new technologies.



Nice to have:

 - Series 7 and 66 or Series 65 licenses.

 - BA/BS degree in finance, economics, or related field.

 - Advanced degrees or designations such as CFP, CPA, CFA

 - Prior experience using Salesforce

 - Prior experience working with custodians such as Fidelity, Charles Schwab, or Pershing Advisor Services



Additional Information:

Savvy Wealth is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive work environment that values diversity and individual contributions.


BENEFITS:

 - Competitive salary and equity package

 - Unlimited PTO + paid company holidays

 - Access to holistic medical, dental, and vision plans

 - Company 401(k) (including Mega backdoor Roth options), Commuter, and HSA/FSA plans

 - NYC office in Union Square

 - Lunch and snacks provided in the office, & dinner if you stay late

 - Access to virtual mental health care (Spring Health) and health concierge (Rightway) to help you find the right care

 - Access to counseling for stress management, dependent care, nutrition, fitness, legal, and financial issues (Guardian WorkLifeMatters EAP)

You’re able to work independently while also thriving in a team environment, helping to build a strong sense of community for both customers and teammates.

Who We're Looking For

• A friendly and enthusiastic team player with a passion for excellent customer service; you're always ready to make your customers' day

• A reliable employee who is able to effectively manage time and priorities, including during busy rush periods where a sense of urgency is necessary

• Passionate about creating delicious coffee, matcha, and other cafe beverages

• A strong independent problem solver with proven multi-tasking and communication skills

• Someone who is curious, adaptable and always willing to learn

• Comfortable working in a team or independently

• Comfortable with cash-handling and maintaining store safety

What You'll Own

• Delight our customers with consistent, welcoming and engaging customer service, taking the opportunity to turn every customer into a regular

• Work within a world-class coffee program using the best coffee equipment and product in the industry to prepare the tastiest drinks

• Complete all training to ensure proper measures are in place to achieve the correct handling of food and beverage to retain its freshness and quality

• Have systems in place to avoid wastage of product with both food and beverage, following and adjusting par levels where needed in line with business peaks and lows

• Maintain Local Department of Health standards at all times

• Full and complete knowledge and adherence to all product, service and brand training playbooks

• Participate in all initiatives with the Operations and Marketing teams to increase foot traffic, new customers, daily sales, and operational profitability and develop a loyal neighborhood customer base

Requirements

• 1+ years’ experience in a customer service position, preferably in hospitality or coffee

• 18+ years of age

• Able to lift 25+ lbs, and to stand for long periods of time

• Availability that meets the needs of our cafes

• Full Time: 30-40 hours per week, 4-5 days per week and must be able to work 2 peak days (peak days: Friday, Saturday, Sunday)

• Weekend and holiday availability preferred

• You must be authorized to work in the U.S.: upon acceptance of a job offer and completion of the Form I-9 with acceptable documents, Blank Street will provide the federal government with employees’ Form I-9 information to confirm authorization to work in the U.S. (a process known as ”E-Verify”)

Benefits & Perks

• A comprehensive Barista accreditation and training program

• Tenure based paid time off

• Commuter benefits

• Sick time

• Complimentary coffee and treats on shift

• Free Blank Street swag

jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

INDUSTRIAL PAINT TECHNICIAN (STARSHIP LAUNCH HARDWARE)

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Sand blast to acceptable industry standards

• Safely operate spray coating equipment to industrial and commercial standards

• Safely operate air tools, pressure feed tanks, and airless pumps

• Brush and roll industrial and commercial coatings

• Perform corrosion control on carbon steel/ stainless steel using pneumatic air tools, needle guns, and scalers

• Safely operate aerial platforms, forklifts, and heavy equipment

• Operate, clean and maintain all painting equipment, including brush, roll, sprayers and electrostatic sprayers, pumps, etc.

• Work with contractors daily to ensure SpaceX standards are being met

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• High school diploma or equivalency certificate

• 1+ years of industrial painting experience

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• 5+ years of industrial painting experience and corrosion control experience

• Experience with NACE, MSDS, and EPA regulation codes or industry standards

• Understanding of heavy equipment safety standards

• Familiarity with paint processes and applications

• Ability to follow detailed instructions

• Self-motivated individual able to work independently or in a team environment and willing to learn

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Ability to pass Air Force background check for Cape Canaveral

• Ability to work the following shift:

• Monday – Friday 6:00am – 4:30pm

• Ability to work nights & weekends when needed to meet critical launch milestones

• Ability to lift heavy objects (up to 25 lbs.) unassisted

• Ability to perform job duties that require standing, kneeling, crouching, twisting upper body, working in cramped positions in small openings and climbing hand over hand

• Ability to work at elevated heights (up to 100 feet)

• Typically exposed to work in extreme outdoor environments – heat, cold, rain

• Work performed in an environment requiring exposure to fumes, odors, and noise

jobs.title: Principal Scientist, Process Chemistry
jobs.description:
Location:  This position may be performed remotely, but requires the flexibility and willingness to travel as needed.

The Opportunity

We’re seeking a Principal Scientist in Process Chemistry to lead drug substance activities for one or more projects within Praxis’ portfolio to support clinical and commercial supply.  Apply your knowledge to design products & processes to support clinical phase testing and then mature them through development to commercial supply.  You are a key leader in the development of drug substance processes for our small molecule products.  You’ll also work closely within the CMC and project teams under Agile management to identify requirements and constraints of our product in order to define a work plan that will lead to the successful manufacturing and creation of a data package to support commercial regulatory submissions.

Primary Responsibilities

• Leads the Process Chemistry Research and Development for one or more projects from early to late phase within Praxis.

• Designs both early phase and late-phase/commercial drug substance process and then leads their demonstration from lab to pilot plant.

• Provides chemistry and technical leadership throughout the lifecycle

• Participates/leads activities to identify final API forms for pharmaceutical development.

• Working closely with formulations, analytical, operations, engineering and quality, expectation to be integrated into the overall CMC team responsible for delivery of clinical and commercial drug substance to Praxis programs.

• Identify, collaborate and lead external CRO, and CDMO organization(s) to achieve deliverables.

• Analyze external experimental data to drive synthetic experimental plans at CROs and CDMO.

• Authoring or co-authoring of regulatory submissions.

• Define manufacturing strategy and execution, including GMP requirements and issue resolution.

• Assessment and application of new trends and concerns in process development, quality and manufacturing to Praxis’ products.

• Manage quarterly budgeting of drug substance relevant activities.

• Contributor to inventions which add value to Praxis and its patients while strengthening our intellectual property position.

Qualifications and Key Success Factors

• Advanced degree or commensurate experience equivalent in Organic Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Engineering or related discipline.

• Minimum of 5+ years of industry experience in CMC specifically for small molecule drug substance.

• A scientific track record or working knowledge in continuous processing, catalysis, biocatalysis and/or high throughput experimentation desirable.

• Strong knowledge of US and EU cGMP requirements and best practices relating to drug substances and drug products.

• Strong knowledge of CMC development across all phases of drug development from initial regulatory filings through registration, validation and launch.

• Experience in working with third-party CRO / CMO partners and associated service providers to develop and manufacturing pharmaceutical products.

• Experience with salt/crystalline form selection preferred.

• Experience with oligonucleotide chemistry is a plus.

• Demonstrates a high level of intellectual curiosity, innovation and creative problem solving with an entrepreneurial spirit; can thrive in an agile environment.

• Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to develop important relationships that include trust and encourage diversity in all its forms.

• Highly organized and detail-oriented with a passion to deliver quality results.

You'll need comfort with screen work, basic hand coordination, and focus. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these functions.

jobs.title: Director, MarTech Operations
jobs.description:
At Constant Contact, we are seriously awesome people who take ownership and make an impact by operating with the mindset, integrity and courage of a small business owner. There’s something so profoundly rewarding about knowing that your work is empowering people everywhere to pursue their dreams.  Here, we all play an integral part in helping business owners, entrepreneurs, non-profits and individuals to succeed by giving them all the help and tools they need to grow online. We’re energized by new challenges and new possibilities-and we’re just getting started!

We are seeking a highly technical, hands-on Director of Paid Media Operations to own the critical data infrastructure that powers our performance marketing. In this role, you will be the ultimate bridge between our marketing strategy and the technical realities of modern ad platforms. You are senior enough to audit our current setup, define our tracking architecture, and guide strategy - but you still love getting your hands dirty in Google Tag Manager and API configurations. If you are passionate about ensuring every dollar spent is backed by flawless data pipelines, this is the role for you.

• The "Player-Coach" Technologist: This is not a media buying role, nor is it a pure IT role. It is a highly specialized position for someone who understands exactly how ad algorithms work and has the technical chops to feed them the right signals (via APIs, Pixels, and GTM) to maximize ROI.

What You'll Do:

Tracking Architecture & Implementation (Hands-on-Keys)

• Own the Tagging Ecosystem: Act as the primary administrator and architect for Google Tag Manager (GTM). Deploy, test, and maintain all conversion pixels, event tags, and custom tracking scripts across our digital properties.

• Master Server-Side Tracking: Lead the implementation and ongoing health of server-to-server APIs to future-proof our tracking against cookie degradation. This includes deep, hands-on work with Meta Conversions API (CAPI), Google Enhanced Conversions, and TikTok Events API.

• Offline Conversion Management: Build and maintain the workflows for uploading offline conversion data (e.g., Google GCLID tracking, CRM stage progression) back into ad platforms to train their bidding algorithms on down-funnel success.

Auditing, QA & Troubleshooting

• Comprehensive Tracking Audits: Regularly audit our existing ad operations infrastructure. Identify data leaks, double-counting issues, broken tags, or misconfigured SDKs, and execute the fixes.

• Pre-Launch Quality Assurance: Establish and enforce a rigorous QA protocol for all new campaigns, landing pages, and website updates to ensure tracking integrity before media dollars are deployed.

• Anomaly Detection: Serve as the technical first responder when data discrepancies occur between ad platforms (Google/Meta) and our internal analytics/CRM systems.

Audience Operations & Data Flow

• First-Party Data Syncing: Oversee the operational flow of 1st-party data from our CRM/Data Warehouse into paid platforms for dynamic audience creation, retargeting, and lookalike modeling.

• Taxonomy & Governance: Define, document, and enforce a strict global UTM taxonomy and naming convention policy to ensure clean downstream analytics.

Cross-Functional Strategy

• Bridge Marketing & Engineering: Act as the core translator between the performance marketing team (who needs the data) and the development/engineering teams (who manage the site code), writing clear technical requirements when developer assistance is needed.

• Ad-Tech Evaluation: Continuously evaluate the evolving privacy landscape (e.g., iOS updates, cookie deprecation) and recommend technical solutions to maintain measurement accuracy.

What You'll Bring:

• 7-10+ years of experience in digital marketing operations, ad operations, or technical marketing, with a proven track record of operating at a senior/architect level while remaining hands-on.

• Deep Expertise in Paid Media Ad Operations: Comprehensive, hands-on knowledge of tracking mechanisms, SDKs, pixel setups, server-side APIs (Meta CAPI, Google GCLID/CAPI workflows), and Tag Management systems (e.g., Google Tag Manager).

• Platform Mastery: Intimate technical knowledge of how major ad networks ingest data (Google Ads, Meta Ads Manager, TikTok Ads, LinkedIn Campaign Manager).

• Technical Fluency: Comfort reading and writing basic web code (HTML, JavaScript, CSS) as it relates to tag firing and data-layer variables.

• Data Literacy: Strong understanding of how CRM data, web analytics (e.g., Google Analytics 4), and paid media data interact. Basic SQL skills for querying audience data is a strong plus.

• An Auditor's Mindset: Relentless attention to detail with a passion for finding the "needle in the haystack" when troubleshooting data discrepancies.

• Exceptional Communication: The ability to explain complex technical tracking issues to non-technical marketing leaders.

Harsco Environmental is seeking a skilled and safety-focused Master Heavy Equipment Mechanic to inspect, diagnose, repair, and maintain a fleet of heavy industrial and mobile equipment operating in a steel mill and industrial site environment. The successful candidate will perform preventative maintenance, troubleshoot complex mechanical and electrical systems, and ensure equipment reliability to support continuous operations. This position requires a hands-on mechanic with strong troubleshooting abilities, a commitment to safety, and the ability to work independently in a demanding industrial environment.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

• Diagnose and repair:Diesel enginesHydraulic systemsElectrical and electronic control systemsPowertrain and drivetrain componentsBraking systemsSteering and suspension systems
• Utilize diagnostic software, laptops, and electronic testing equipment to identify equipment faults and perform repairs.
• Perform troubleshooting of equipment and other heavy equipment manufacturers' machines using OEM diagnostic software and service manuals.
• Conduct welding, cutting, fabrication, and component replacement as necessary.
• Complete work orders, inspection reports, and maintenance records accurately and timely within maintenance management systems.
• Perform field repairs in industrial operating areas and respond to equipment breakdowns to minimize downtime.
• Inspect equipment for safety, operational readiness, and compliance with company standards.
• Maintain inventory of tools and communicate parts requirements to supervisors and parts personnel.
• Collaborate with operations teams to identify equipment issues and develop effective repair solutions.
• Follow all company safety policies, lockout/tagout procedures, and environmental regulations.
• Participate in continuous improvement initiatives focused on equipment reliability and operational efficiency.

Required Qualifications

• High school diploma or GED required.
• Minimum of 5-7 years of experience repairing heavy equipment, construction equipment, mining equipment, or industrial mobile equipment.
• Strong mechanical aptitude and troubleshooting skills.
• Experience with diesel engine repair and maintenance.
• Ability to read and interpret service manuals, hydraulic schematics, wiring diagrams, and technical documentation.
• Proficiency using hand tools, power tools, and diagnostic equipment.
• Valid driver's license required.
• Ability to work overtime, weekends, and on-call shifts as business needs require.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with heavy equipment diagnostics and repairs.
• Experience working in steel mills, industrial plants, mining operations, or heavy manufacturing environments.
• Knowledge of PLC-controlled systems and industrial electrical troubleshooting.
• Welding and fabrication experience.
• Commercial Driver's License (CDL) is a plus.

Physical Requirements

• Ability to lift up to 50 pounds regularly and up to 75 pounds occasionally with assistance.
• Ability to climb ladders, stairs, and heavy equipment.
• Ability to work in confined spaces and elevated work areas.
• Ability to stand, walk, bend, kneel, crouch, and reach for extended periods.
• Ability to work outdoors and in varying weather conditions.

Work Environment

• Industrial steel mill and heavy manufacturing environment.
• Exposure to dust, noise, vibration, heat, cold, and moving equipment.
• Required use of personal protective equipment (PPE), including hard hat, safety glasses, steel-toe boots, hearing protection, and high-visibility clothing.
• Fast-paced environment supporting critical production operations.

Key Competencies

• Mechanical troubleshooting and diagnostics
• Heavy equipment maintenance and repair
• Hydraulic and electrical systems expertise
• Safety awareness and compliance
• Problem-solving and critical thinking
• Time management and organization
• Teamwork and communication
• Reliability and accountability

Additional Information

We offer competitive benefits, including health insurance, life insurance and disability plans, as well as a 401k with company matching.

[https://app.ashbyhq.com/api/images/user-content/890b2b79-9c1c-4227-a7e9-f66faa7d1198/cf2636a3-8541-4f2d-8c88-7c9cff17dca5/Personal_Pivot%20Employees.png]




ABOUT US

Every company that scales lives or dies by its procurement function. It manages the vendor relationships that keep operations running, the financial guardrails that prevent overspend, and the supply chain resilience that determines whether a company survives a crisis or folds under one. And yet, the people doing this work spend 80% of their time in spreadsheets. Not because they lack ambition, because the tools haven't changed in 25 years.


Pivot is building the AI operating system for procurement: enterprise-grade infrastructure that hands the manual grind to AI agents so procurement teams can do what they were actually hired to do, shape the strategic future of their companies. Our platform combines intake, approvals, vendor management, invoice matching, and ERP integrations in a single AI-native platform. 


We've lived this frustration firsthand. We built Pivot because we couldn't find what we needed, and because we believe procurement shouldn't be the last function to enter the AI era. It should be the first.


The adventure started mid-2023 with three founders, former C-levels from fintech unicorns (Qonto, Swile, and Nuxeo). We’ve since raised $40M in a Series B round, totaling our funding to $70M, coming from tier-1 investors. We’ve built a team of 70, are operating across 25+ countries, and are trusted by enterprise leaders like DoorDash, Lemonade, Wolt, and Flix


We're looking for smart, execution-driven people who care about building something exceptional.




YOUR ROLE

Pivot is growing its enterprise business, we're hiring a Senior Enterprise BDR in New York to open doors at some of the world's largest organisations.

This isn't a high-volume, transactional BDR role, and there's no playbook to simply follow. You'll own a portfolio of strategic accounts across the US, build your own target lists, follow the right signals and create opportunities with senior stakeholders in Procurement, Finance and the wider business.

Working closely with our Enterprise Account Executives, you'll build account strategies, find the right entry points and turn cold accounts into qualified pipeline. What matters most is knowing how to navigate large, complex organisations.

Why now? Our US market is largely untapped: you'll start almost from scratch on high-potential accounts, with real autonomy, and help our sales leaders shape Pivot's outbound motion.




WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

 - Own your accounts. Build your target lists and run self-sourced outbound prospecting across a portfolio of strategic enterprise accounts.

 - Map the organisation. Identify stakeholders, influencers, decision-makers and potential champions, and understand each account's priorities, technology landscape and transformation initiatives.

 - Go multi-threaded. Build engagement across several personas and business units rather than relying on a single contact.

 - Plan with your AE. Partner with Enterprise Account Executives on account plans and the best route into priority organisations.

 - Lead with a reason. Spot business triggers (leadership changes, M&A, cost programmes, new regulation) and turn them into timely, commercially relevant outreach.

 - Use every channel. Engage Director, VP and C-level buyers by phone, email, LinkedIn, events and creative outbound, with cold calling as a core part of your approach.

 - Tailor the message. Write outreach built around each stakeholder's priorities, not generic sequences.

 - Create qualified pipeline. Turn early conversations into qualified opportunities and run the discovery call. You'll be measured on pipeline quality (conversion to Stage 2, opportunity value) rather than meetings booked, with the ultimate goal of driving closed-won revenue alongside your AE.

 - Stay in the deal. Help your AE bring new stakeholders into the sales cycle, secure referrals and keep momentum through to close.

 - Keep the CRM sharp. Capture account intelligence, stakeholder maps and activity accurately, and share what you learn with the wider Revenue team.

 - Shape the motion. Help build a predictable, repeatable outbound engine, from qualification criteria to best practices.




REQUIREMENTS

 - 2+ years in B2B SaaS outbound (BDR, SDR or business development), 100% outbound, prospecting into large enterprises, with a proven track record of self-sourcing qualified pipeline

 - Experience with complex deals: 500+ employee accounts, multiple stakeholders and ACVs above $50K (ideally $100K+).

 - Strong account-mapping skills and a clear understanding of how enterprise buying committees work.

 - Confidence engaging Director, VP and C-level stakeholders, with cold calling as a core prospecting channel.

 - Commercial curiosity and sharp communication: you understand a business before you reach out, and tailor your message to each persona.

 - Self-driven and collaborative: you own your accounts and work closely with AEs, Marketing and RevOps

 - The ability to balance highly personalised account work with consistent outbound execution.

 - Native English, our business language.

 - Strong attention to detail and excellent listening skills.




NICE TO HAVE

 - Outbound pipeline generation into Procurement, Finance, Operations or Transformation functions.

 - BDR experience in Procurement Tech, FinTech, Source-to-Pay, Procure-to-Pay or adjacent enterprise software.

 - Prospecting into regulated or complex industries such as Financial Services, Insurance or Energy.

 - Experience in a fast-growing SaaS business where processes and playbooks are still evolving.

 - Additional languages.

No procurement or fintech background? No problem: we'll train you on Pivot, our market and our tools.




YOUR SALES MINDSET

 - You are a master of enterprise accounts: you can take a large enterprise account and work out how to get inside it. You know the obvious contact isn't always the right one, and that enterprise opportunities rarely come from a single conversation.

 - You are a strategic thinker who approaches your portfolio like a business: researching each account, building a stakeholder map and prioritising high-potential accounts.

 - You are confident and credible at C-suite level, able to engage procurement directors and CFOs through thoughtful outreach and by picking up the phone.

 - You are a hunter at heart: hungry, driven and persistent. Rejection doesn't discourage you. You keep momentum, test new angles, and know how to re-engage accounts that have gone quiet.

 - You are commercially sharp: rather than simply asking for meetings, you find the reason Pivot should be talking to an organisation now, and build your outreach around it.

 - You are a collaborative teammate who uplifts those around you: partnering closely with your AE, sharing knowledge with the Revenue team, and contributing to a culture of high performance.

 - You like solving problems and making complex things look simple.

 - You always want to keep learning and you are comfortable with confronting ideas.

 - You enjoy the pace of a fast-growing startup and want to bring the best of yourself to it.

 - You want to share good vibes with smart and caring co-workers.




WHAT YOU WILL GET

 - A competitive base salary of $77K–91K, plus uncapped commission

 - A package of employee stock option plan (ESOP)

 - Medical plan

 - Life insurance

 - Retirement plan

 - 2 days of remote work per week

 - An office in Midtown Manhattan, a two-minute walk from the Empire State Building, at the heart of our US expansion

 - The richness of a multicultural and international team (more than 15 nationalities).

 - A unique chance to grow with a fast-scaling innovator

jobs.description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

An overview of this role

This role is 100% remote and will be based in the US and Canada.

As a Small and Medium Business (SMB) Account Executive (New Business), you'll focus exclusively on acquiring new GitLab customers. You'll own a territory of free GitLab users, trial users, engaged leads, and cold prospects, combining inbound and outbound sales to build relationships and business cases from scratch. You'll lead consultative sales conversations that connect customer challenges to GitLab's value and help shape the playbook for winning new customers.

jobs.title: Managing Director, Fund Finance and Legal
jobs.description:
About Equi

Equi exists to give investors superior tools to own their financial future. We bring institutional-quality alternative strategies, the small-to-midsize, hard-to-replicate kind that are genuinely difficult to access, to the wealth channel and institutional investors. Our ambition is to be a leading alternatives investment partner, and to elevate every portfolio we touch. We build multi-strategy funds and custom mandates for some of the best independent multi-family offices and advisory firms in the country, and we pair deep manager selection with portfolio construction most of our competitors cannot run.

Momentum is the reason this seat exists now. We just launched the largest client in our history and have several more signed or close to it, with a multiple of today's assets as the near-term target. We are roughly ten people, which means this hire shapes the function rather than inherits it. Our funds invest through several layers of vehicles, onshore and offshore. That structure is what lets us deliver these strategies to this channel, and it makes the accounting and reporting genuinely complex. The finance function here is more demanding than the size of the firm suggests.

About the Role

We are hiring a Managing Director of Fund Finance and Legal to own the finance function for the fund complex and the management company. You own the numbers the firm publishes: the NAV cycle and the reconciliation behind it, fund expenses and the annual budget, treasury and cash, audit and tax, and the corporate financials that go to the CEO and the board. You also own the financial and legal architecture of every new vehicle we launch. This is a senior finance leadership seat reporting to the CEO, based in New York, hybrid with three days a week on site.

Fund finance and fund operations are peer functions here. Our Head of Fund Operations owns the operational execution of the close, investor transactions and capital activity. You own the financial standards, the controls and the reporting those processes run against. The two of you are jointly accountable for the complex, and the partnership is the job.

Three things make this different from a controller seat at a larger shop. We outsource our books and records on purpose, so your job is not to re-do that work. It is to understand every number well enough to catch an error before it reaches an investor, to decide the firm's position when two sources disagree, and to hold the whole network to a standard. The seat also carries real legal ownership: you take point with outside counsel on fund launches, structuring and documentation, and you read the governing documents closely enough to know what they commit us to. And we are deliberately tech-forward. When something recurring is manual, we expect you to reach for a tool rather than absorb the work. You do not have to build everything yourself, but you do have to be capable of it.

Culture

Equi is a team-first environment where transparency and healthy debate are integral to our success. We operate with a flat structure: ideas win on merit, not seniority, and every team member is expected to argue a position and change their mind when the evidence warrants. Nobody here is narrowly role-specific. When there is an adjacent fire, you step in.

We are deliberate about being tech-forward. People here build their own tools rather than waiting on a roadmap, and that expectation applies to this seat as much as any other.

What You'll Do

Financial Reporting and the Close

 - Own the NAV cycle across every vehicle, the reconciliation between our own view and our providers', and final sign-off before anything reaches investors

 - Own the close calendar and the standard it is held to

 - Run the annual fund expense budget, the allocation policy across vehicles, and the re-billing between fund and management company

 - Partner with the CEO on corporate financials, burn, runway and board reporting

Treasury, Audit, Tax and Regulatory

 - Own the firm's cash position across operating and fund accounts, at banks and prime brokers, current rather than reconstructed at month end, with the controls and approval authority around every wire

 - Serve as the firm's counterpart to the auditor on the annual audit, and stay accountable for the tax cycle landing, with the preparer doing the work

 - Hold the firm's regulatory and compliance positions alongside our compliance partner, including fund documents, side letters and investor agreements as the complex grows

Fund Launches, Structuring and Legal

 - Own the financial and legal architecture of every new vehicle: structure, fee terms, governing documents, entity formation, registrations, account opening and administrator onboarding

 - Take point with outside counsel throughout, while keeping the existing complex running as we launch

Partnership with Fund Operations and the Provider Network

 - Set the financial standards and controls that capital activity, the investor register, investor onboarding and the day-to-day close run against, jointly accountable with our Head of Fund Operations

 - Hold the administrator, outsourced fund-ops team, auditor, tax preparer, outside counsel, prime brokers and banks to a service standard, and renegotiate when they miss

Financial Systems and Records

 - Build toward one financial source of truth rather than several competing copies

 - Put documented procedures in place that do not depend on any one person, and own the tooling that makes the rest of this run

Who You Are

We are looking for a finance leader with real depth in fund accounting, fluency with fund legal documents, and a genuine appetite for using AI and technology to run the function better.

Required

 - Deep Fund Accounting and Fund Operations: Eight to twelve years running or overseeing the financial operation of a fund complex, at a fund administrator, hedge fund, multi-strategy fund, private-markets manager, or outsourced fund-CFO practice. You know the NAV cycle cold and can look at a draft NAV and find the error before anyone else does. Multi-layered structures are where you are most comfortable.

 - Fund Legal Fluency: You have worked closely with fund counsel on launches, structuring and documentation. You can read a private placement memorandum, a side letter and a subscription agreement and know what they commit the firm to, and you can run a formation without routing every question to counsel.

 - AI Fluency: You already use AI as a working tool to draft, reconcile, analyze and build small things that remove recurring work. You can tell us specifically what you have built with it in the last six months and what it changed, and you are visibly excited about where this goes.

 - Technical Range Beyond Excel: Scripts, automations, small internal applications, or a willingness to pick up a new tool over a weekend. You do not need to be an engineer, but a career of only Excel and an ERP will not be a fit.

 - Small-Firm Operating Experience: You have worked somewhere lean enough that you did the work yourself, not only directed it, and you are comfortable going as deep as the problem requires while building the function out.

 - Provider Oversight: You have managed administrators, transfer agents, auditors, tax preparers, outside counsel, prime brokers and banks, and you know where the hand-offs break.

 - Controls and Judgment: You are precise, you close loops, and you treat investor capital and confidential information with appropriate seriousness.

 - Ownership: You take a problem to a finished state without being managed to it, and you say so plainly when something is wrong.

Preferred

 - Multi-strategy and multi-vehicle structures, especially layered arrangements where a single allocation splits across several vehicles and has to be attributed back cleanly

 - A legal background or qualification, or depth built through years of sitting across the table from fund counsel

 - Offshore vehicles and the audit and filing cycle that comes with them

 - ERISA and plan-asset monitoring

 - A CPA, or equivalent depth arrived at another way

Why This Seat Is Interesting

Equi is at the stage where a finance function stops being a set of processes and becomes a system. The foundations are in place: a strong provider network, a clean structure, real scale. The next chapter is building the leverage on top of it and deciding what this function looks like as the platform doubles. If you want to shape a function at the point where the decisions still matter, there are not many seats like it at this stage.

jobs.title: Vehicle Test and Launch Engineer II
jobs.description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

NEUTRON

Neutron is a medium-lift launch vehicle being developed by Rocket Lab, a publicly traded end-to-end space company. The rocket can deliver the mega constellations of tomorrow, enable interplanetary payloads, and support human spaceflight. As a reusable platform, Neutron will deliver a very cost-effective and reliable launch solution leveraging Rocket Lab’s proven history with Electron – the third most launched rocket, worldwide, in 2024. If you’re interested in joining an incredible team in a fast-paced and rewarding environment, this is your opportunity.

VEHICLE TEST AND LAUNCH ENGINEER II

The Test and Launch Operations team at Rocket Lab is responsible for testing, launch, and mission operations of Electron and Neutron launch vehicle. Starting with stack testing through pre-launch processing, launch operations, and on-orbit operations. Integrated Operations is also responsible for configuration, checkout, and operation of related facilities, equipment, and infrastructure.

The Test and Launch Engineer will have a detailed understanding of disciplines related to testing and operations. The Engineer will have or develop skills in multiple operational roles, including roles where they will direct, mentor, and train other operators. In addition, the Engineer II will take a leadership/ownership role in testing and operations projects and process or tool development efforts.

WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO:

• Develop, integrate, and test mechanical systems relating to the Electron and Neutron launch vehicles

• Oversee the configuration and checkout of launch vehicle systems

• Lead and manage testing projects for launch vehicle systems, including static testing and integrated stage hot fire testing

• Mentor and train other operators within the Integrated Operations team on launch vehicle mechanical and propulsion systems

• Develop Concept of Operations (CONOPS) and Human-Machine Interfaces (HMIs) related to vehicle stage and engine hardware

• Perform real-time troubleshooting to resolve test/operations issues

• Author, review and carry out operations procedures

YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS AS A VEHICLE TEST AND LAUNCH ENGINEER II:

• Bachelor Degree in Engineering (preferably Aerospace, mechanical, electrical or mechatronic engineering)

• 2+ years of experience in engineering design, test and/or operations, in the focus of mechanical or propulsion systems

• 6+ years of experience will be considered in lieu of a degree

THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE:

• Experience with launch vehicles or spacecraft including integration, testing, launch, or mission operations

jobs.title: Senior/Staff Software Engineer, Connected Systems
jobs.description:
WHAT TO EXPECT

Heron Power is a startup building cutting-edge power electronics for the 21st-century grid. We aim to debottleneck the growth of electricity generation and consumption with scalable, innovative, and cost-effective hardware and software solutions, accelerating the electrification of everything.

Our first goal is to build better converters (inverters & rectifiers) to connect large-scale renewables, storage, and loads to the grid. Heron’s leadership team is made up of seasoned veterans who have designed and shipped gigawatts of power conversion products.

We believe no one person knows everything. We learn together, build together, and solve hard problems from first principles. You’ll work in a fast-moving, deeply technical environment where ownership and impact are real.




JOB OVERVIEW

As a Senior/Staff Software Engineer, you will contribute to building scalable Connected Systems software, including telemetry pipelines, fleet management, system fault analysis, diagnostics, configuration management, and secure firmware updates for grid-connected energy systems.

You will participate in design, build, and operation of key components of Heron Power's Connected Systems platform. You'll work across edge devices, cloud infrastructure, data pipelines, backend services, and user-facing applications used to monitor, diagnose, and operate grid-connected energy systems.

You will own meaningful components and services, contribute to production-critical capabilities, and collaborate closely with embedded, hardware, test, manufacturing, and frontend engineers to help deliver reliable, secure, and scalable end-to-end systems.

We're looking for a hands-on engineer who builds production software, solving complex distributed systems problems, and working across multiple engineering disciplines. You have experience delivering substantial software systems and owning technical outcomes from component design through operation.




WHY THIS ROLE IS DIFFERENT

This role owns critical components of larger software platform that enables smart functionality across Heron products and systems. You will create software that will run on energy-critical infrastructure deployed in challenging environments with limited connectivity and limited access. You will contribute to enabling Heron Care – industry first support and maintenance program ensuring continuous unit operation and supportability for extended periods of time. You will work on data systems that capture fleet-scale telemetry since device inception through decades of field operations.




HOW YOU WILL CONTRIBUTE



CORE RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Build scalable backend services and data platforms for industrial IoT deployments.

 - Build telemetry ingestion, processing, storage, and analytics pipelines supporting fleet monitoring and system fault analysis.

 - Develop services and workflows for diagnostics, remote troubleshooting, asset lifecycle tracking, and over-the-air firmware updates.

 - Implement APIs, event-driven services, and data models that enable reliable integration across Connected Systems, Firmware, Manufacturing, and System Test.

 - Contribute to software quality through code reviews, testing strategies, observability, and operational excellence.


COLLABORATION

 - Work closely with embedded software engineers on Cabinet Gateway integration, telemetry collection, and firmware management.

 - Collaborate with Manufacturing and System Test teams to improve data availability, traceability, and operational workflows.

 - Partner with DevOps and infrastructure teams on CI/CD, deployment automation, and observability.

 - Support development of customer-facing tools and dashboards for monitoring system performance and health.

 - Share technical input with engineering leadership on roadmap and prioritization decisions.




WHAT YOU WILL BRING



MUST-HAVE REQUIREMENTS

 - 7+ years of professional software engineering experience, including ownership of significant components of a distributed system.

 - Experience contributing to complex software products from design through production deployment.

 - Experience building, or contributing to, industrial IoT, telemetry, fleet management, or other large-scale connected systems.

 - Strong experience designing and implementing backend services in Python, Golang, Rust, Java, or similar languages.

 - Experience building telemetry ingestion, stream processing, or event-driven systems using Kafka or cloud-native equivalents.

 - Solid understanding of APIs, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and data platform design.

 - Experience collaborating across firmware, hardware, manufacturing, test, and software teams.

 - Strong debugging and problem-solving skills in production environments.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with fault detection, diagnostics, or prognostics systems.

 - Familiarity with industrial networking, SCADA, or edge computing architectures.

 - Experience with frontend technologies such as React.

 - Experience building systems supporting remote device management and firmware updates.

If you are passionate about technology and enjoy working in a fast-paced environment, we would love to hear from you. Join us in accelerating the electrification of everything at Heron Power.

Heron Power provides competitive compensation (salary and equity) and benefits. The salary for this role ranges from $163,000 to $207,000 per year.

MISSION

Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear. 

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.




ROLE PURPOSE:

We are looking for an experienced Sonographer to join our clinical team in Miami. This role is responsible for independently administering abdominal and vascular ultrasounds as part of Neko's full-body preventive health scan.



You will perform and interpret studies across both modalities, producing accurate, same-session reports — working autonomously within defined escalation protocols. You will work alongside our Echocardiographer and closely with the Miami Medical Area Lead to ensure findings are integrated into each member's complete health picture.



This is a full-time role based at our clinics in Miami, Florida.




WHAT YOU'LL DELIVER IN THE FIRST 6–12 MONTHS:



 - Perform abdominal ultrasound examinations including liver, gallbladder, spleen, kidneys, and aorta in accordance with AIUM guidelines and Neko clinical protocols.

 - Perform peripheral vascular studies including lower and upper limb arterial and venous assessments.

 - Independently complete scans partnering with radiology partners and Neko clinical leads

 - Collaborate with the multidisciplinary clinical team to incorporate findings into full-body preventive health assessments.

 - Follow Neko's escalation protocols consistently and document findings in the clinical record accurately.

 - Liaise directly with our consulting specialists when escalation or second opinion is required.

 - Participate in quality assurance activities including audit and peer review.

 - Contribute to continuous improvement of ultrasound protocols as the US clinical model develops.




MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:



 - ARDMS certification in Abdomen (RDMS-AB) and vascular certification (RVT or RDMS-VS) required.

 - Minimum two years of post-certification independent reporting experience across abdominal and vascular modalities.

 - Strong communication skills — able to explain findings clearly to members without medical backgrounds and to clinical colleagues.

 - Commitment to high clinical standards and active engagement in ongoing professional development.

 - Eligible to work in the United States.




PREFERRED:



 - Additional ultrasound certifications (IE: musculoskeletal or cardiac)- Familiarity with integrating findings into broader preventive or longitudinal health assessments.

 - Experience in a high-volume or technology-forward clinical setting.

 - Prior involvement in clinical research, protocol development, or health technology initiatives.

 - If you do not have these skills at hire, an interest in developing cardiac ultrasound skills over time (training support available) is strongly desired.

The Team

The Construction and Infrastructure organization delivers the facilities, infrastructure, and construction projects required to support Valar's mission. The team manages planning, execution, and delivery of complex capital projects while ensuring quality, safety, and operational readiness.

The Role

As Infrastructure Project Manager, you will manage the execution of infrastructure and facility projects from planning and design through construction, commissioning, and turnover. You will coordinate internal stakeholders, design consultants, contractors, vendors, and project teams to deliver projects safely, on schedule, within budget, and in accordance with technical and operational requirements. Success in this role is measured by schedule and budget performance, forecast accuracy, design and construction quality, disciplined change-order and RFI management, safety performance, and smooth commissioning and turnover.

• Manage infrastructure projects from concept through design, construction, commissioning, and closeout.

• Develop and maintain project scope, schedule, budget, and execution plans, including milestones, deliverables, and decision requirements.

• Lead design reviews, constructability reviews, and value-engineering activities, and resolve multidisciplinary design conflicts.

• Partner with construction managers, general contractors, and trade contractors to monitor progress and resolve field issues affecting cost, schedule, quality, or safety.

• Develop and maintain budgets and cost forecasts, tracking commitments, actual costs, contingencies, and change orders.

• Maintain critical-path schedules, identify recovery opportunities, and coordinate procurement of long-lead equipment, escalating cost and schedule risks early.

• Work closely with Infrastructure Design, Construction, Facilities, Operations, Procurement, Finance, EHS, IT, and other teams to translate business and operational requirements into actionable project requirements aligned with broader site plans.

jobs.title: Infrastructure Engineer Intern
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Arcesium is a global financial technology firm that solves complex data-driven challenges faced by some of the world’s most sophisticated financial institutions. We constantly innovate our platform and capabilities to meet tomorrow’s challenges, anticipate the risks our clients encounter, and design advanced solutions to help our clients achieve transformational business outcomes.

Financial technology is a high-growth industry as change and innovation continue to disrupt the status-quo and prompt major transformation. Arcesium is at a particularly interesting time in our own growth as we look to leverage our successfully established market position and expand operations in pursuit of strategic new business opportunities. We value intellectual curiosity, proactive ownership, and collaboration with colleagues, and we empower you to meaningfully contribute from day one and accelerate your professional development.

Position Summary
Arcesium seeks an exceptional Infrastructure Intern to join our Technology team for the summer. The Infrastructure team is responsible for all aspects of Arcesium’s cloud computing environment. The goal of our summer internship program is to give exposure to the projects and environment at Arcesium to students with an interest in systems infrastructure studying computer science, computer engineering, and other STEM majors. Both undergraduate and graduate students of all years are welcome and encouraged to apply. The Infrastructure Intern will work directly with experienced full-time engineers responsible for providing the core infrastructure required to run our customer-facing platform, while learning about how to build and scale a modern cloud-based enterprise SaaS business. The role requires a mix of systems engineering and software development.

Responsibilities

- Help implement the next-generation architecture and automation that manages the cloud environment for our SaaS platform
- Contribute to the design and implementation of our platform's infrastructure and likely getting exposure to Linux engineering, cloud computing (AWS), Kubernetes / Docker, and Site Reliability Engineering (SRE)
- Work closely with our application teams to optimize integration between our software and infrastructure
- Assist the Infrastructure team with various projects. Examples of past projects include writing Slack bots used by all developers at Arcesium, building a CI job autoscaler to optimize the performance, reliability, and cost of CI jobs, introducing new self-service capabilities into our customer-facing products, and adding new features into our secrets manager. Potential projects for this summer will focus on the intersection of infrastructure and developer experience.

Qualifications

- The ideal candidate will possess a broad grasp of theory, practice, and interest in areas such as automation, Linux, networking, security, cryptography, cloud computing, systems administration, and software development
- Ability to code, along with strong thinking and communication skills, both written and verbal, is required
- Technologies we use include: Linux, Kubernetes, Docker, Python, Haskell, Java, Kerberos (MIT/Windows), DNS (BIND), AWS (SQS, SNS, EC2, VPC, Route 53, EBS, S3, DynamoDB), SSH, IPSec, Ansible, NFS, Git
- Ability to use GenAI tools for enhancing productivity

The expected monthly salary for this position is $10,000. Our compensation package also includes a one-time housing stipend.

The applicable salary paid to a successful applicant will be determined based on multiple factors including without limitation the nature and extent of prior experience and educational background.

Arcesium's Personal Data Privacy Notice for Candidates is linked here.

Recruiting Security
Emails from genuine Arcesium recruiters who are employees of the company will always come from the @arcesium.com domain. In some cases, you may also be contacted by independent search firms engaged to recruit on our behalf; emails from their employees should always come from their firm's applicable domain. We'll never ask for your banking information or any payment as part of the recruiting process. If something seems off or you're contacted by an unexpected third party, please reach out to us at careers@arcesium.com (US/UK), careers-india@arcesium.com (India) or careers-europe@arcesium.com (Portugal/Sweden).

Arcesium is an equal opportunity employer.
