jobs.title: Staff Security Architect
jobs.description:
Why Sony Interactive Entertainment?

Sony Interactive Entertainment isn’t just the Best Place to Play — it’s also the Best Place to Work. Sony Interactive Entertainment (SIE) is the company behind the PlayStation brand. As a subsidiary of Sony Group Corporation, we’re part of a proud legacy of innovation and excellence. SIE is a dynamic technology company, delivering cutting-edge hardware and network services to more than 100 million people and an entertainment leader, home to some of the most beloved and recognizable intellectual properties (IP) in the world. Our role at SIE is to create and nurture the experiences under the PlayStation brand, a name synonymous with entertainment excellence and creativity.

Sony Interactive Entertainment

Security Architecture | Cloud | AI Security | Enterprise Platforms

We are seeking a Staff Security Architect to help shape and secure the next generation of enterprise, cloud, platform, and AI-enabled technology. This role combines deep security architecture expertise with strong engineering judgment and the ability to influence technical direction across complex, global environments. The successful candidate will partner with engineering, infrastructure, product, and security teams to identify systemic risk, develop scalable security patterns, and guide secure adoption of emerging technologies, including generative AI and agentic systems.

Key Responsibilities

• Design, review, and approve security architecture for enterprise, cloud, SaaS, platform, and application environments, balancing business objectives, engineering constraints, and risk.

• Lead cloud security architecture across AWS, Google Cloud, and hybrid environments, including identity, network security, data protection, logging and monitoring, key management, workload isolation, security posture management, and the effective use of native and third-party cloud security controls.

• Define and review security architecture for SaaS and PaaS platforms, including identity federation, privileged access, tenant configuration, data protection, API and integration security, logging, third-party risk, and secure adoption of enterprise SaaS services.

• Drive security throughout the software delivery lifecycle, including source control, CI/CD pipelines, build systems, artifact repositories, infrastructure as code, secrets management, code and artifact signing, software provenance, deployment automation, and security controls for developer platforms.

• Lead security architecture for AI-enabled systems, including generative AI, large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, AI agents, model-serving platforms, and AI-assisted developer workflows.

• Design mitigations for risks such as prompt injection, insecure tool use, excessive agency, sensitive-data disclosure, model or supply-chain compromise, unsafe output handling, and abuse of AI services.

• Define security requirements for AI data, models, prompts, embeddings, vector stores, APIs, tools, and agent identities, including least-privilege access, secrets management, encryption, isolation, provenance, logging, monitoring, and lifecycle controls.

• Architect and improve identity, authentication, authorization, network security, key management, cryptography, application security, and production security controls across complex environments.

• Identify security design gaps in existing and proposed systems; translate findings into practical architecture improvements, reference patterns, hardening standards, preventative controls, and responsible automation that improves repeatability and operational effectiveness.

• Provide technical leadership across multi-disciplinary teams, clearly articulating risks, tradeoffs, and recommended solutions to engineering leaders, business stakeholders, and audiences without a security background.

Required Qualifications

• 15+ years of relevant experience in security architecture, security engineering, product security, cloud security, infrastructure security, or related disciplines, with demonstrated leadership at senior or staff level.

• Deep knowledge of security architecture principles across cloud, application, network, identity, platform, infrastructure, and enterprise environments.

• Hands-on experience designing or securing cloud-based and containerized environments, including major cloud platforms such as AWS or Google Cloud.

• Strong understanding of modern identity and access management, PKI, OAuth/OIDC, SAML, TLS, VPNs, secrets management, key management systems, cloud KMS, and HSMs.

• Expertise in network and application security controls such as WAFs, NGFWs, segmentation, DMZ design, DDoS mitigation, load balancing, proxies, intrusion detection/prevention, and host-based controls.

• Experience with secure software development, threat modeling, CI/CD and developer platforms, application security, and engineering mitigations across the software lifecycle.

• Working knowledge of AI/ML security concepts and the ability to evaluate security risks in generative AI, LLM, and agentic system architectures, including data flows, trust boundaries, model access, and tool integrations.

• Strong critical thinking, risk prioritization, communication, and influence skills, with the ability to lead through ambiguity and work effectively across global, cross-functional teams.

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Engineering, Information Security, or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience securing AI/ML platforms, generative AI applications, model gateways, RAG architectures, vector databases, or agentic workflows in production environments.

• Experience with AI security evaluation, red teaming, adversarial testing, model abuse testing, or control validation for AI-enabled systems.

• Experience securing large-scale Linux, distributed, multi-tenant, or high-availability production environments.

• Development or automation experience in Python, C++, Java, or similar languages.

• Recognized technical leadership through patents, publications, open-source contributions, conference participation, teaching, or security community involvement.

• Penetration testing, adversarial security, or attacker-minded design experience.

• Master's degree or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Mathematics, Engineering, Information Security, or a related field.

Please note, Sony Interactive Entertainment conducts background checks at the offer stage for all new employees (which may include criminal background checks for some roles) and will need to process personal information to support these checks.

Please refer to our Candidate Privacy Notice for more information about what personal information we collect, how we use it, who we share it with, and your data protection rights.

jobs.title: Local Pneumatic Bulk Driver
jobs.description:
HOURLY PAY + Weekly O/T : $28.36/hr  + $5,000 Sign-On Bonus – paid out over your first year!

M-F Day Shift - Home Daily!

• Steady schedule
• Robust vacation package - up to 1 week in first year, and 2 weeks after year one
• Paid sick time after 1 year
• 401k Plan + Company Match​​​​​​​

TBC is seeking an experienced Class A CDL Pneumatic Bulk Truck Driver, based out of our Waterloo, IN facility. The Bulk Driver is responsible for the safe and efficient delivery of cement powder and other related products in both rural and urban environments in all weather conditions.

Here is some insight into what your day-to-day will entail:

• Drive company-owned trucks in a professional manner to transport and deliver products or other materials
• Operate equipment, such as truck cab computers, CB radios, and telephones to exchange necessary information with dispatch, supervisors, or other drivers
• Pre-trip and post-trip inspections of vehicle and trailer to ensure safety as a priority
• Completes daily DOT pre-trip inspections and required logs. Submits and verifies accuracy of all documentation.
• Responsible for the cleanliness, upkeep, and routine maintenance checks of assigned vehicle. Reports issues, accidents, and damage to the leadership team.
• Maintains and submits all trip-related receipts and expenses.
• Obtains and maintains accurate delivery authorization and pickup documentation. Verifies shipment documents such as load tickets, bills of lading and work orders.
• Drive trucks to weigh stations when appropriate along routes to document weights and to comply with state regulations
• Occasional flat bed deliveries when available

Delivery

• Maneuver trucks into loading or unloading positions, following signals from loading crew
• Check all load-related documentation to ensure that it is complete and accurate
• Obtain receipts or signatures for delivered goods and collect payment for services when required

Required Skills/Abilities:

• Adaptable: Able to anticipate and respond to unexpected situations (traffic, weather, road conditions, onsite restrictions).
• Time-management: Committed to timely deliveries and providing quality service to our customers.
• Organized and detail-oriented: Maintains accurate records for documents, gas cards, receipts, and load tickets.

Qualifications:

jobs.title: Security GRC Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE:

Join Rightway as a Security GRC Manager, a role that owns and matures our GRC function. You will enhance our policies and procedures, streamline workflows, mature our risk management program, own our integrated SOC 2 + HITRUST attestation as we scale, and lead the GRC team.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

• Team Leadership: Lead and mentor a small GRC team, setting priorities, reviewing work, and growing the function alongside the business.

• Control Library Development: Own and evolve our unified control library, maintaining mappings across SOC 2, SOC 1, and the latest HITRUST version, and addressing gaps or inefficiencies as the organization and framework requirements change.

• Audit Ownership: In partnership with Engineering, IT, People, and Finance, lead the audit program for control requirements and evidence production, proactively in anticipation of SOC 1, SOC 2/HITRUST, and customer audits.

• Data Privacy and Protection: Partner with Legal as a key stakeholder in the Data Privacy program, including HIPAA/HITECH, BAAs, data privacy and protection impact assessments, incident/breach analysis, and data handling requirements.

• AI Governance: Own and mature the AI governance program modeled after ISO/IEC 42001, including the AI risk register, Statement of Applicability, and AI risk assessments for internal use cases. Respond to customer and partner AI governance questionnaires, and maintain alignment to emerging requirements such as the Colorado Automated Decision-Making Technology Act (ADMTA).

• Contract security and privacy review: Review and negotiate security, privacy, data protection, incident notification, audit rights, AI, and related language in customer and vendor agreements.

• Control Monitoring: Monitor, measure, and report on control effectiveness for security and compliance in Drata, maintaining continuous control monitoring and evidence collection, and adjusting strategy and implementation as needed.

• Policy Enhancement: Collaborate cross-functionally to improve policies and related procedures, boosting operational efficiency, control maturity, security, and compliance

• Business Continuity Planning: Lead business continuity planning and testing, with a focus on a Business Impact Analysis (BIA) informed program.

• Third Party Risk Management: Revamp and execute a flexible yet thorough Third Party Risk Management (TPRM) program, keeping a keen eye on data security and technical risk, not just compliance.

• Risk Management: Own the security risk management program, participating in preparation, discussion, tracking (risk register), and remediation of enterprise risks within your sphere of influence, in addition to annual risk assessments activities.

• Training Programs Development: Engage with organizational stakeholders to develop and implement effective security and compliance training programs.

• Customer Trust: Own and maintain the customer assurance program, including the security questionnaire and RFP response process, trust center content, and the tooling that supports timely, accurate responses for the Proposal Unit and prospective clients.

WHO YOU ARE:

• 5-10 years of related work experience.

• Maintains a certification relevant to the role (e.g, CISSP, CISA, CISM).

• Personally led SOC2 with HITRUST CSF certification in a high growth environment and understands how to mature controls consistent with organizational maturity and capacity.

• Familiarity with AI governance frameworks (e.g., ISO/IEC 42001) and the risk considerations of AI systems that process sensitive data.

• Experience leading or mentoring GRC analysts, with the ability to set priorities, review work, and grow the function alongside the business.

• A deep understanding of risk assessment methodology, HIPAA, and HITECH, including the practical distinction between covered entity and business associate obligations. Comfortable negotiating and redlining BAAs and conducting four-factor breach risk assessments alongside Privacy and legal.

• Passionate advocate for governance, risk, and compliance, believing that these are not merely check box activities, but vital tools that significantly improve security posture and protect the organization.

• Possess an intermediate to advanced understanding of the Software Development Life Cycle and of IT and security tooling (Jamf, CrowdStrike, Arctic Wolf, Wiz, Serval, Knowbe4, Drata) as it relates to controls (e.g. AWS, Okta, JIRA, GIT/GITHUB).

• Ability to perform qualitative and quantitative risk assessment.

EXTRA CREDIT:

• Experience with joint SOC 2/HITRUST attestations.

• A blend of deep, technical and compliance knowledge and experience.

COMPENSATION:  $144,000 - $175,000 annually, in addition to bonus and equity

Compensation offered will be determined by geographic location, experience, and qualifications.

CYBERSECURITY AWARENESS NOTICE

In response to ongoing and industry-wide fraudulent recruitment activities (i.e., job scams), Rightway wants to inform potential candidates that we will only contact them from the @rightwayhealthcare.com email domain. We will never ask for bank details or deposits of any kind as a condition of employment.

ABOUT RIGHTWAY:

Rightway is on a mission to harmonize healthcare for everyone, everywhere. Our products guide patients to the best care and medications by inserting clinicians and pharmacists into a patient’s care journey through a modern, mobile app. Rightway is a front door to healthcare, giving patients the tools they need along with on-demand access to Rightway health guides, human experts that answer their questions and manage the frustrating parts of healthcare for them.

Since its founding in 2017, Rightway has raised over $300mm from investors including Khosla Ventures, Thrive Capital, Francisco Partners, and Tiger Global. We’re headquartered in New York City, with satellite offices in Denver and Dallas. Our clients rely on us to transform the healthcare experience, improve outcomes for their teams, and decrease their healthcare costs.

HOW WE LIVE OUR VALUES TO OUR TEAMMATES:

We’re seeking those with passion for healthcare and relentless devotion to our goal. We need team members that embody our core values:

1) We are human, first
Our humanity binds us together. We bring the same empathetic approach to every individual we engage with, whether it be our members, our clients, or each other. We are all worthy of respect and understanding and we engage in our interactions with care and intention. We honor our stories. We listen to—and hear—each other, we celebrate our differences and similarities, we are present for each other, and we strive for mutual understanding.

2) We redefine what is possible
We always look beyond the obstacles in front of us to imagine new solutions. We approach our work with inspiration from other industries, other leaders, and other challenges. We use ingenuity and resourcefulness when faced with tough problems.

3) We debate then commit
We believe that a spirit of open discourse is part of a healthy culture. We understand and appreciate different perspectives and we challenge our assumptions. When working toward a decision or a new solution, we actively listen to one another, approach it with a “yes, and” mentality, and assume positive intent. Once a decision is made, we align and champion it as one team.

4) We cultivate grit
Changing healthcare doesn’t happen overnight. We reflect and learn from challenges and approach the future with a determination to strive for better. In the face of daunting situations, we value persistence. We embrace failure as a stepping stone to future success. On this journey, we seek to act with guts, resilience, initiative, and tenacity.

5) We seek to delight
Healthcare is complicated and personal. We work tirelessly to meet the goals of our clients while also delivering the best experience to our members. We recognize that no matter the role or team, we each play a crucial part in our members’ care and take that responsibility seriously. When faced with an obstacle, we are kind, respectful, and solution-oriented in our approach. We hold ourselves accountable to our clients and our members’ success.

Rightway is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer that believes in the strength of diverse thought, beliefs, backgrounds, and education. We foster an inclusive culture where differences are celebrated to drive the best business decisions possible. We do not discriminate on any basis protected by applicable law. jobs.title: Contractor, Robotics Lab Technician
jobs.description:
Your Impact at LILA

Lila's Next Gen Robotics team builds and integrates the robotic systems that power our development lab. As a contract Robotics Lab Technician, you will design, build, and integrate those systems, combining off-the-shelf components like robot arms, mobile bases, and sensors (cameras, lidars, and similar) into new configurations.

You will do real CAD design work, creating the mounts, fixtures, and adapters that let these components work together, then producing them through 3D printing and building them out by hand. You will also handle the electrical and controls work needed to wire everything up and get it running.

This is a practical, in-lab role for someone comfortable designing a solution and then getting hands-on with the robot.

What You'll Be Building

• Design parts, mounts, fixtures, and adapters in CAD to integrate off-the-shelf robotic components

• Take measurements, iterate on fit and function, and produce parts via 3D printing and light fabrication

• Assemble and integrate robotic hardware from your own designs or engineering drawings

• Wire and mount sensors, actuators, and control components, including cable routing and connector termination

• Configure motor controllers, I/O, and sensor interfaces, and debug basic control issues alongside engineers

• Install, calibrate, and troubleshoot robotics sensors and subsystems during bring-up and integration

• Maintain and upgrade lab robots, document builds and fixes, and keep the lab safe and organized

What You'll Need to Succeed

• Hands-on experience working on or around robots, such as arms or mobile bases, with a practical understanding of how they function

• Solid working ability in CAD (SolidWorks, Fusion 360, or similar), able to design parts from scratch

• Comfortable taking measurements, iterating on fit and function, and producing parts via 3D printing

• Familiarity with common robotics sensors (cameras, lidars, or similar), including installation, wiring, and basic troubleshooting

• Basic hands-on electrical skills: wiring, soldering or crimping, using a multimeter, reading simple schematics

• Practical, adaptable problem-solver who is comfortable in a fast-moving, hands-on lab environment

• Good communicator who can work closely with engineers across mechanical, electrical, and software domains

Bonus Points For

• Some exposure to controls hardware (motor controllers, I/O boards, actuators) and willingness to learn more

• Experience designing mounts, brackets, or adapters to integrate off-the-shelf hardware components

• Prior experience in a robotics lab, research lab, or similar hands-on hardware environment

• Familiarity with ROS or other robotics software or middleware

• Experience with 3D printers (setup, calibration, basic troubleshooting)

• Any background in mechatronics, electromechanical work, or a related technical field

About LILA

Lila Sciences is building Scientific Superintelligence™ to solve humankind's greatest challenges. We believe science is the most inspiring frontier for AI. Rather than hard-coding expert knowledge into tools, LILA builds systems that can learn for themselves.

LILA combines advanced AI models with proprietary AI Science Factory™ instruments into an operating system for science that executes the entire scientific method autonomously, accelerating discovery at unprecedented speed, scale, and impact across medicine, materials, and energy. Learn more at www.lila.ai.

Guided by our core values of truth, trust, curiosity, grit, and velocity, we move with startup speed while tackling problems of historic importance. If this sounds like an environment you'd love to work in, even if you don't meet every qualification listed above, we encourage you to apply.

We’re All In

Lila Sciences is committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status.

Information you provide during your application process will be handled in accordance with our Candidate Privacy Policy.

A Note to Agencies

Lila Sciences does not accept unsolicited resumes from any source other than candidates. The submission of unsolicited resumes by recruitment or staffing agencies to Lila Sciences or its employees is strictly prohibited unless contacted directly by Lila Science’s internal Talent Acquisition team. Any resume submitted by an agency in the absence of a signed agreement will automatically become the property of Lila Sciences, and Lila Sciences will not owe any referral or other fees with respect thereto.

jobs.description:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known.

Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us.

About the Team:

The Launch team operates at the intersection of every major aspect of Terran R, from stages and payloads to ground systems, launch, landing, and refurbishment. The Cape is the only place where you see it all come together, offering a level of exposure and responsibility unmatched elsewhere in the program. This is where first flights happen, where history is built on top of history, and where the scale of what's underway is unlike anything in modern aerospace. The mission stays the same, but the work evolves with every milestone: from first launch to reuse, high-cadence operations, and beyond. If you're looking to define what's next in space launch and write a new playbook, not just repeat what’s already been done, this is where it happens.

About the Role:

• Define electrical system architecture, technical requirements, and design approaches for complex launch and processing facilities, providing technical leadership across multiple projects and development phases.

• Lead the design and integration of electrical systems ranging from 22.5 kV to 120 V, including power generation, distribution, protection, controls, sequencing, redundancy, and mission-critical infrastructure.

• Establish electrical engineering standards, design practices, and technical criteria that improve system reliability, maintainability, safety, and scalability across current and future launch facilities.

• Resolve complex, cross-disciplinary engineering challenges involving electrical infrastructure, launch systems, construction, operations, and vehicle interfaces, using engineering first principles to guide high-impact technical decisions.

• Provide technical oversight for major equipment selections, design reviews, construction packages, subcontractor deliverables, installation, commissioning, and system acceptance while identifying and mitigating technical and program risks.

• Serve as a technical resource for engineers and cross-functional teams by reviewing critical designs, developing technical talent, and partnering with engineering and program leadership to shape long-term facility and infrastructure strategy.

About You:

• Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering or a related field and 8+ years of relevant electrical engineering experience.

• Experience establishing electrical system architecture and independently leading complex engineering efforts involving power generation, distribution, protection, controls, or mission-critical infrastructure.

• Experience applying engineering first principles to resolve technically ambiguous or high-impact problems spanning multiple systems, disciplines, or project phases.

• Experience providing technical leadership across the full project lifecycle, including requirements development, design, procurement, construction, commissioning, troubleshooting, and operations.

• Experience developing or influencing engineering standards, design practices, technical specifications, or architecture decisions used across multiple projects or teams.

• Experience communicating complex technical decisions, risks, and tradeoffs to engineering teams, contractors, operations partners, and senior stakeholders.

Nice to haves but not required:

• Experience developing electrical architecture or technical standards for orbital launch, aerospace, utility, industrial, or other mission-critical facilities.

• Experience designing and commissioning medium- to high-power electrical systems involving redundancy, protection coordination, power quality, or high-availability operations.

• Experience applying NFPA, military, NASA, or similar regulatory and technical requirements to complex electrical infrastructure.

• Experience providing technical mentorship or design leadership to engineers working across multiple electrical projects or systems.

Successful candidates must clear a background check administered by the US government to obtain clearance for on-site work at our government partner location in Cape Canaveral, Florida.

jobs.title: Senior Engineer II, Robotics Mechanical Design
jobs.description:
Your Impact at LILA

Our Platform Evaluation team tests and benchmarks alternative robotics platforms, including mobile manipulators, AMRs/AGVs, and other form factors, against our current production baseline. The team builds custom mobile manipulators by combining off-the-shelf components from different AMR and robot arm manufacturers, for example mounting one or more arms from a given vendor onto an AMR base from another.

As the Robotics Mechanical Design Engineer, you will own the mechanical design of these custom configurations end to end: mocking up multiple iterations (different arm brands, mounting positions, and configurations), modeling them fully in CAD, and preparing designs for simulation and physical build.

You will work closely with the Platform Evaluation engineers, who validate designs in simulation (NVIDIA Isaac Sim) and in physical testing once built. This is a hands-on mechanical and mechatronic design role, not a robotics software or controls position.

What You'll Be Building

• Design and iterate mounting and integration concepts combining robot arms with AMR/AGV base platforms

• Produce multiple design options per platform combination for evaluation

• Model custom mobile manipulator configurations in CAD, including brackets, structural supports, and interface hardware

• Run mass, center-of-gravity, and payload analysis to keep configurations within manufacturer specifications

• Design cable, hose, and connector routing between the arm, end effector, and AMR base

• Prepare simulation-ready CAD models and specifications (exportable URDF/mesh geometry) for Isaac Sim validation

• Document design decisions, tolerances, and assembly procedures, and support physical build and integration

What You'll Need to Succeed

• Mechanical or mechatronic design experience in a production, commercial, or applied R&D setting, ideally involving robotics or automated equipment

• Strong proficiency in 3D CAD software (SolidWorks, Fusion 360, Onshape, or similar)

• Experience designing mechanical mounts, brackets, or structural interfaces for hardware integration

• Understanding of payload, mass properties, and center-of-gravity considerations for robotic arms on mobile bases

• Familiarity with robot arm and AMR specifications, including mounting interfaces, payload limits, and reach envelopes

• Comfortable iterating quickly, producing and revising multiple design options rather than one final design upfront

• Strong documentation habits, with the ability to communicate design intent and constraints to a non-mechanical audience

Bonus Points For

• Experience preparing CAD models for downstream simulation use, exporting clean geometry at a level of detail suited to URDF/mesh conversion

• Experience with robot arms and AMRs specifically, rather than general industrial equipment

• Familiarity with ROS2/URDF conventions

• Experience with NVIDIA Isaac Sim or other robotics simulation tools

• Background in industrial design for warehouse automation, logistics robotics, or manufacturing equipment

• Experience with rapid prototyping methods such as 3D printing, sheet metal, and machining for early design iterations

Compensation

We offer competitive base compensation with bonus potential and generous early-stage equity. Your final offer will reflect your background, expertise, and expected impact.

U.S. Benefits. Full-time U.S. employees receive a comprehensive benefits program including medical, dental, and vision coverage; employer-paid life and disability insurance; flexible time off with generous company wide holidays; paid parental leave; an educational assistance program; commuter benefits, including bike share memberships for office based employees; and a company subsidized lunch program.

International Benefits. Full-time employees outside the U.S. receive a comprehensive benefits program tailored to their region. USD salary ranges apply only to U.S.-based positions; international salaries are set to local market.

Expected Base Salary Range

$136,800—$190,634 USD

About LILA

Lila Sciences is building Scientific Superintelligence™ to solve humankind's greatest challenges. We believe science is the most inspiring frontier for AI. Rather than hard-coding expert knowledge into tools, LILA builds systems that can learn for themselves.

LILA combines advanced AI models with proprietary AI Science Factory™ instruments into an operating system for science that executes the entire scientific method autonomously, accelerating discovery at unprecedented speed, scale, and impact across medicine, materials, and energy. Learn more at www.lila.ai.

Guided by our core values of truth, trust, curiosity, grit, and velocity, we move with startup speed while tackling problems of historic importance. If this sounds like an environment you'd love to work in, even if you don't meet every qualification listed above, we encourage you to apply.

jobs.title: Pipefitter II
jobs.description:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known.

Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us.

About the Team:

The Launch team operates at the intersection of every major aspect of Terran R, from stages and payloads to ground systems, launch, landing, and refurbishment. The Cape is the only place where you see it all come together, offering a level of exposure and responsibility unmatched elsewhere in the program. This is where first flights happen, where history is built on top of history, and where the scale of what's underway is unlike anything in modern aerospace. The mission stays the same, but the work evolves with every milestone: from first launch to reuse, high-cadence operations, and beyond. If you're looking to define what's next in space launch and write a new playbook, not just repeat what’s already been done, this is where it happens.

About the Role:

As a Fitter II on the Launch Team, you will fabricate, fit, and install critical piping systems that support the Terran R launch site, including process piping, utility systems, and other ground support infrastructure. You will work with experienced fitters, engineering, fabrication, and construction teams to complete piping installations safely, accurately, and in accordance with project requirements. Your hands-on pipe fitting skills and attention to detail in both shop and field environments will contribute to building reliable systems that support launch operations.

About You:

• You have 2+ years of professional pipe fitting, fabrication, construction, or mechanical experience, including hands-on experience with industrial piping systems

• You can read and interpret isometric drawings, P&IDs, blueprints, spool drawings, dimensions, elevations, and piping specifications to support piping fabrication and installation

• You can measure, lay out, cut, bevel, grind, drill, fit, align, and prepare pipe, fittings, flanges, valves, supports, and other piping components using appropriate tools and equipment

• You can fabricate and install carbon steel, stainless steel, or similar piping systems while following established specifications, quality requirements, and safety procedures

• You can identify common fit-up, alignment, dimensional, and installation issues and collaborate with experienced team members to resolve field challenges

• You can coordinate safely with other trades and operate applicable shop and field equipment, which may include forklifts, reach lifts, man lifts, and rigging equipment, while performing the physical tasks required in an industrial work environment

Nice to haves but not required:

• Experience with industrial piping fabrication, installation, maintenance, testing, commissioning, shutdowns, or turnaround work

• Experience working with carbon steel, stainless steel, alloy, or other piping materials and associated equipment connections

• Previous experience in aerospace, power generation, shipbuilding, petrochemical, pharmaceutical, semiconductor, or another regulated industrial environment

• Experience supporting hydrostatic or pressure testing, flushing, system turnover, commissioning, or troubleshooting of piping systems

Successful candidates must clear a background check administered by the US government to obtain clearance for on-site work at our government partner location in Cape Canaveral, Florida.

Food has lost its soul to modern convenience. And with it, it has lost the power to nourish, inspire, and connect us. So in 2018, CookUnity was founded as the first-of-its-kind platform that connects the world with the source of truly great food: chefs. Today, CookUnity delivers 50 million meals a year from the industry’s best chefs to homes all over the country. Fresh. Ready-to-eat. And crafted with the passion that nourishes body and soul.

Unwilling to stop there, CookUnity is expanding beyond delivery to become an ever-innovating marketplace focused on our singular mission: empower Chefs to nourish the world.

If that mission has you hungry in more ways than one, you’ve found the right job posting.

About the Role

The Sustainability Operator plays a key role in ensuring that daily waste‑management procedures are executed correctly across the NEW YORK facility. This role supports the operational execution of recycling, compost, waste audits, and donation processes, helping maintain clean, compliant, and efficient waste‑diversion systems.

The Zero Waste Operator is responsible for carrying out daily walkthroughs, completing waste‑audit forms, preparing and coordinating donations, and ensuring correct sorting and disposal of materials in all kitchens and work areas. This role provides essential operational support to the facility by monitoring compliance, identifying contamination, and reinforcing correct waste‑handling behaviors among staff.

Key responsibilities include executing daily waste audits, preparing food waste for donation or internal use, coordinating donation pick‑ups with partner organizations, maintaining Green Stations, and ensuring all supplies needed for proper waste diversion are available and correctly used. This role ensures that Zero Waste procedures are followed consistently and effectively, contributing to CookUnity’s environmental goals and operational priorities.

Summary

Execute daily operational tasks related to recycling, compost, waste audits, and donation management within the LA facility, ensuring compliance with processes and sustainability standards.

Responsibilities:

• Daily Waste Audits : Perform daily trash audits across workstations and document findings.

• Correct Waste Disposal : Ensure proper waste disposal procedures are followed in all kitchens.

• Food Waste Handling : Classify, weigh, and dispose of food waste, including donations, compost, garbage, and family meals.

• Facility Walkthroughs — Conduct daily walkthroughs of kitchens, green stations, fulfillment, and market areas; complete the DAILY AUDIT BIN FORM to identify contamination.

• Contamination Control — Check recycling and compost streams to ensure they are free of incorrect materials.

• Material Sorting — Separate and move recyclable and compostable materials according to facility standards.

• Donation Management : Collect, weigh, record, and pack donations; receive partners and hand off prepared products.

• Food Waste Preparation: Condition and prepare food waste for donation or internal reuse (back to market).

• Food Donation support: Coordinate donation pick‑ups with partnered non‑profit organizations.

• Daily Reporting: Complete daily trackers for recycling, compost, and donation volumes.

• Zero Waste Compliance: Follow all safety, cleanliness, and Zero Waste process standards.

• Operational Feedback: Provide daily feedback to staff to reinforce correct waste‑sorting behaviors.

• Green Leader Support: Support team members as a Green Leader, promoting “Go Green” practices.

• Waste Diversion Supplies: Ensure stations have the correct supplies (stickers, posters, bins) for proper waste diversion.

• Green Station Maintenance: Coordinate with the cleaning team to keep the Green Stations clean and in order.

General Schedule and Workdays

Full Time (5 days a week - 36 to 40 hs weekly).

PM shift: 2:00 pm to 10:00 pm.

Available to work on the weekends.

Qualifications

• Operational Experience: Previous experience in warehouse, food production, cleaning, or other hands‑on operational roles. Comfortable working in kitchens, warehouse areas, and food production spaces.

• Physical Requirements: Ability to safely lift and move 20 lbs or more throughout the shift..

• Basic Reporting Skills : Ability to complete daily trackers and simple audit forms.

• Communication Skills: Ability to give clear feedback to staff and communicate deviations or contamination findings. Spanish and English

• Interest in Waste Reduction: Genuine interest in recycling, composting, waste diversion, or environmental practices (no prior experience required).

• Language: Basic English required; Spanish is a strong plus.

JOB REQUIREMENT

• Bilingual – Spanish and English (mainly spoken).

• Basic knowledge of Google Docs.

• Experience operating both: Forklift and Pallet Jack.

All final pay rates will be determined by candidates experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities of the applicant, internal equity, and alignment with market data.

$18—$18 USD

This position supports production, overburden removal, haulage, stockpile management, road maintenance, and other mining activities while adhering to all safety, environmental, and operational standards.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

• Operate mining equipment including haul trucks, dozers, excavators, loaders, graders, water trucks, and other support equipment.

• Safely transport ore, waste rock, overburden, and other materials throughout the mine site.

• Maintain haul roads, access roads, dumps, stockpiles, and work areas.

• Load and unload materials efficiently while minimizing equipment wear and damage.

• Monitor equipment performance and promptly report mechanical issues or safety concerns.

• Follow mine plans, production schedules, radio communication protocols, and supervisor instructions.

• Assist with drilling, blasting support, reclamation, and earthmoving activities as required.

• Adhere to all MSHA regulations, company safety policies, and environmental requirements.

• Participate in safety meetings, training programs, and continuous improvement initiatives.

• Maintain accurate production, inspection, and operational records.

• Work effectively with dispatchers, maintenance personnel, supervisors, and fellow operators.

Required Qualifications

• High school diploma or GED preferred.

• Minimum 2 years of heavy equipment operating experience; surface mining experience preferred.

• Knowledge of safe operating practices for large mobile mining equipment.

• Ability to read and interpret mine maps, procedures, and operating instructions.

• Valid driver's license with acceptable driving record.

• Ability to obtain and maintain required mine site certifications and site access credentials.

• Strong commitment to safety and operational excellence.

Preferred Qualifications

• MSHA Part 46 or Part 48 Surface Miner Training.

• Experience operating CAT, Komatsu, Hitachi, Liebherr, or similar mining equipment.

• GPS machine control experience.

• Basic mechanical aptitude and equipment troubleshooting skills.

• Experience working in large-scale aggregate, quarry, copper, coal, gold, or industrial mineral mining operations.

Physical Requirements

• Ability to sit and operate equipment for extended periods.

• Ability to climb ladders, steps, and access equipment safely.

• Ability to work outdoors in varying weather conditions, dust, mud, and noise.

• Ability to lift up to 50 pounds occasionally.

• Ability to work day, night, weekend, holiday, and rotating shifts as required.

Work Environment

• Surface mining operation with exposure to heavy equipment traffic, dust, vibration, and changing weather conditions.

• Requires strict adherence to safety procedures and personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements.

• May require overtime and travel between surface mine locations.

Key Competencies

• Safety Focus

• Situational Awareness

• Equipment Operation Expertise

• Reliability and Attendance

• Teamwork and Communication

• Problem Solving

• Attention to Detail

• Production Efficiency

This role requires compliance with all applicable safety regulations, personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements, and Loenbro's Environmental Health and Safety (EH&S) policies.

Our team is extremely talent-dense. Among our founding team, we have world-class competitive programmers, former founders, and leaders from companies at the cutting edge of AI including Scale AI, Palantir, Cursor, Waymo, Tesla, Lunchclub, Modal, Google DeepMind, and Nuro.

Building Devin is just the first step—our hardest challenges still lie ahead. If you’re excited to solve some of the world’s biggest problems and build AI that can reason on real-world tasks, apply to join us.


ROLE MISSION

Devin writes and runs code, uses tools, takes actions in real customer systems, and operates for hours without a human in the loop. Safety here is not a research paper; it is whether an agent behaves correctly in production, millions of times a day. You will be a founding member of Cognition's safety team, reporting to the Head of Safety. You will build the evaluations and red-teaming that gate every release, develop alignment methods that shape how our models are trained, and work directly with the agent team on how Devin plans, acts, and asks for help. This is a hands-on research engineering role for someone who wants their safety work to run in the loop of a real agent, not sit in a benchmark.




WHAT YOU'LL ACCOMPLISH

 - Build agentic safety evals: Design and run evaluations for the failure modes that matter for autonomous agents: unsafe actions, prompt injection, data exfiltration, sandbox escape, reward hacking, and misuse. Make them fast enough to run on every model and product release.

 - Red-team Devin: Attack the agent and its harness systematically. Find the failures before customers do and turn them into fixes and regression tests.

 - Develop alignment methods: Work with post-training on reward modeling, preference data, constitutional approaches, and other techniques that make the model safer without making it worse at the job.

 - Shape the agent harness: Partner with the agent team on permissions, oversight, and escalation: when Devin should act, when it should ask, and how it should explain itself.

 - Publish and share: Contribute to Cognition's external safety work through papers, evals, and open methods where it makes sense.
   
   


EXCEPTIONAL CANDIDATES HAVE DEMONSTRATED

 - Safety or alignment research experience: Hands-on work on evaluations, red-teaming, alignment, or interpretability at a frontier AI lab or in published research. You have built things that changed how a model was trained or deployed.

 - Agentic systems understanding: You know how agents fail in practice: tool misuse, specification gaming, long-horizon drift, adversarial inputs. You have measured it or have concrete ideas about how to.

 - Strong engineering fundamentals: Proficiency in Python and PyTorch (or JAX). You can build eval infrastructure, run experiments at scale, and read the training and inference code.

 - Empirical rigor: You design clean experiments, report results honestly, and know the difference between a real improvement and noise.

 - Comfort with adversarial thinking: You enjoy breaking systems and are good at it.

 - Relevant industry experience: Prior experience at a frontier AI lab, applied AI company, or developer tools company.

 - Advanced degree: PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Physics, Mathematics, or a related discipline; or equivalent industry research experience.


EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities throughout the hiring process - please let us know if you need any.

a. Lead and manage OE tire development projects from initiation through production release.

g. Support Global Tire Testing (GTT) in the development of customer-specific test methods, as required.

h. Prepare and collect required documentation and drawings to obtain customer engineering approval and support PSW sign-off.

i. Coordinate activities with internal and external stakeholders to ensure flawless OE tire launches and production readiness.

Business Support:

a. Support customer account activities and technical reviews for current and future OE tire development programs.

b. Develop and maintain effective, trust-based relationships with key customer decision-makers focused on long-term value creation.

c. Support RFQ activities and Five-Year Planning initiatives as requested by the KAM or Technical Account Manager.

d. Gather and communicate customer, competitor, and market intelligence to support business growth strategies and alignment with OE customer needs.

e. Support management of R&D budgets by promoting cost-effective practices, minimizing non-value-added activities, and leveraging lessons learned across programs.

f. Assume additional responsibilities as needed to support changing customer requirements, business priorities, market conditions, and organizational objectives.

g. Support the development and execution of technical strategies that strengthen Continental's competitive position and future business opportunities.

h. Develop and coordinate customer-focused activities, including technical meetings, technology demonstrations, driving events, facility visits, and advanced development projects to enhance customer perception of Continental's technical capabilities, execution quality, and innovation leadership.

Quality:

a. Maintain internal and external quality management processes, including creation and management of customer complaint records within applicable systems and databases.

b. Share lessons learned across cross-functional teams to prevent recurrence of quality issues.

c. Support Account Quality Managers, Regional Quality Managers, and Technical Account Managers as required.

d. Monitor customer satisfaction and quality performance metrics, provide regular status updates to account management, and support corrective action plans to address identified gaps.

e. Support conformity-of-production testing activities and communicate results to account management.

f. Monitor end-of-line quality data, including tire uniformity, balance, and visual inspection results, and collaborate with plant and central quality teams to drive continuous improvement.

g. Collect and analyze warranty performance data for assigned products and review findings regularly with customers and account management.

h. Support customer audits and facility visits by coordinating activities, participating in plant audits, tracking action plans, completing customer self-assessments, and evaluating external warehouses and third-party tire and wheel assembly providers as required.

i. Support plant and central quality teams in maintaining customer-specific certifications and quality requirements, including BIQS, Q1, VQE, and similar standards.

j. Share responsibility with the PDT Group Leader, Technical Account Manager, and Key Account Manager for compliance with IATF 16949 requirements.

k. Support APQP activities, including coordination and submission of PPAP documentation to customers and launch management teams.

l. Participate in quality planning and problem-solving activities, including FMEA, 8D, Control Plans, and GT PoMS documentation and related IT systems.

m. Provide required customer documentation to internal Continental stakeholders.

n. Translate Customer Specific Requirements (CSR) and Product Specific Requirements (PSR) into internal specifications and PoMS documentation.

o. Serve as the key user and subject matter resource for customer portals and related IT systems.

WHAT YOU BRING TO THE ROLE

• Bachelors Degree in Engineering
• 2+ years related professional experience
• 1+ year of experience in tire or chassis development, tire or chassis testing and/or automotive engineering
• Project management skills and experience in leading projects (preferably with an international focus)
• International work experience and/or work experience in an intercultural environment for several years

jobs.title: Head of Safety
jobs.description:
WE ARE AN APPLIED AI LAB BUILDING END-TO-END SOFTWARE AGENTS.

We're the makers of Devin, the first AI software engineer. 

Our team is extremely talent-dense. Among our founding team, we have world-class competitive programmers, former founders, and leaders from companies at the cutting edge of AI including Scale AI, Palantir, Cursor, Waymo, Tesla, Lunchclub, Modal, Google DeepMind, and Nuro.

Building Devin is just the first step—our hardest challenges still lie ahead. If you’re excited to solve some of the world’s biggest problems and build AI that can reason on real-world tasks, apply to join us.


ROLE MISSION

Devin is one of the most capable autonomous agents in production. It writes and runs code, uses tools, takes actions in real customer systems, and operates for hours without a human in the loop. That makes it one of the most important places in the industry to get safety right, and one of the few where safety work ships to millions of developers rather than staying in a paper. You will build Cognition's safety function from the ground up: the research agenda, the evaluation and red-teaming program, the deployment policies, and the team. You will work directly with the researchers training our models and the engineers building the agent harness. This is a hands-on role for someone who has done serious safety or alignment work at a frontier lab and wants to apply it where agents actually operate.




WHAT YOU'LL ACCOMPLISH

 - Own safety end to end: Set the safety strategy for Devin and the models behind it, and own the outcomes.

 - Build the evaluation program: Design evals and red-teaming for agentic risk: unsafe actions, prompt injection, data exfiltration, sandbox escape, reward hacking, and misuse. Make them part of every model and product release.

 - Shape training and the agent harness: Partner with pre-training, post-training, and agent teams so safety is built into how models are trained and how Devin plans, acts, and asks for help.

 - Set deployment policy: Define what Devin is and is not allowed to do, how permissions and oversight work, and how we handle the gray areas, in a way that holds up with enterprise customers.

 - Build the team and the external voice: Hire and lead safety researchers and engineers. Represent Cognition's safety work with customers, policymakers, and the broader research community.
   
   


EXCEPTIONAL CANDIDATES HAVE DEMONSTRATED

 - Frontier lab safety or alignment experience: Hands-on work on safety, alignment, evaluations, or red-teaming at a frontier AI lab. You have shipped safety work that affected real models or products.

 - Agentic systems depth: You understand how agents fail in practice: tool misuse, specification gaming, long-horizon drift, adversarial inputs. You have ideas about how to measure and mitigate it.

 - Research credibility: A track record of published or widely used safety research, evals, or methods. An advanced degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related field is a plus.

 - Technical fluency: Comfortable in Python and in the training and inference stack. You can read the code, run the evals, and argue with researchers on the details.

 - Builder, not reviewer: You have started or scaled a safety function and prefer shipping mitigations to writing memos about them.

 - Judgment under uncertainty: You can make clear calls on deployment risk with incomplete information and explain them to engineers, executives, and customers.


EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

Cognition is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for candidates with disabilities throughout the hiring process - please let us know if you need any.

You will set the scientific direction, build the team, and ensure our methods, specifications, stability programs, and control strategies are ready for each stage of development, from pre-IND work through potential NDA/MAA approval.

 - Extend enablement beyond account executives to serve Solutions Architects, Customer Success Managers, Global Services, and channel partners. Align frameworks so every customer-facing team speaks the same language.

 - Lead and stabilize a very talented team that has been through significant organizational change. Provide clear vision, invest in development, and build a culture where people do the best work of their careers.



We're looking for candidates who have:

 - 10+ years of experience in sales, customer success, enablement, revenue operations, GTM operations, or a related operational function within complex B2B SaaS companies

 - Built or materially scaled a function, program, or operational capability from early stage. You have a track record of creating structure where there was none.

 - Demonstrated ability to thrive in ambiguity: you've operated in environments where the strategy was iterative, the infrastructure was incomplete, and you had to build while leading. You bring resilience and grit, not just skill.

 - Hands-on operational instinct. You are an operator first, and you build systems, design processes, introduce automation, and do the work yourself when that's what the situation demands. You are not looking for a role where you set strategy and delegate execution.

 - Direct experience working with or inside a strong sales enablement function. You understand what good looks like, even if your career hasn't been spent exclusively in enablement.

 - Experience managing geographically distributed teams across multiple time zones, and a passion for developing people

 - Product curiosity and enough understanding of product-to-market motions to maintain credibility with Product Marketing and Product teams.

 - Strong communication skills and the ability to build trust with senior leaders, sales managers, and cross-functional partners quickly.



Nice to have experience:

 - Knowledge of Force Management, Command of the Message, or MEDDPICC.

 - Prior experience as a quota-carrying account executive or in a direct selling role.

 - Experience working in or with financial services, the public sector, or compliance-related industries (financial crime, AML/CFT, payments, trading systems).

 - Experience with enablement technology platforms (LMS, conversation intelligence, AI role-play tools).

 - Experience supporting a business model transition (for example, from subscription to consumption pricing).

 - Interest in cryptocurrency, blockchain, and related technologies, or a deep curiosity and willingness to learn.

AI at Chainalysis
AI is not a feature at Chainalysis - it is a new way of working. One that turns instructions into work done, and helps us move faster than the threats we're built to counter, and we expect our employees to take ownership of the output and ensure quality. As the world's most trusted blockchain analytics platform, Chainalysis sits at a rare intersection of proprietary data, regulatory relationships and crypto expertise that makes it uniquely placed to shape and lead the next era of AI-driven intelligence - and we expect everyone here, regardless of role, to be an active part of it.

AI fluency is tied directly to how we measure performance and how we plan to win. There is no substitute for your own curiosity. We provide the tools, workflows, and space to experiment - but the expectation is that you develop these capabilities yourself, bring ideas, and collaborate across teams to reinvent the way work gets done. We are not using AI to do less. We are using it to do what was never possible before.



About Chainalysis

Chainalysis is the blockchain data platform, making it easy to connect the movement of digital assets to real-world services. Powered by deep blockchain data and AI, organizations can investigate illicit activity, manage risk exposure, and develop innovative market solutions built on the industry's most trusted blockchain intelligence. Our mission is to build trust in blockchains, blending safety and security with an unwavering commitment to growth and innovation.



You belong here. 

At Chainalysis, we believe that diversity of experience and thought makes us stronger. With both customers and employees around the world, we are committed to ensuring our team reflects the unique communities around us. We’re ensuring we keep learning by committing to continually revisit and reevaluate our diversity culture.

We encourage applicants across any race, ethnicity, gender/gender expression, age, spirituality, ability, experience and more. If you need any accommodations to make our interview process more accessible to you due to a disability, don't hesitate to let us know. You can learn more here https://go.chainalysis.com/rs/503-FAP-074/images/Interview%20Accommodations%20Request.pdf. We can’t wait to meet you.

jobs.title: Sr. Technical Leader (NYC)
jobs.description:
If you think your skills, experience and aspirations make you a good match for this position, we encourage you to apply.

ABOUT THE ROLE

You will perform in the role of Sr. Technical Leader for a large office and/or region and be part of a multi-disciplinary leadership team to provide quality oversight and technical leadership on projects.  This involves executing strategic initiatives and advising teams to achieve objectives. You will make significant contributions toward development of firm-wide technical processes and improvements.

HERE'S WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Manage and monitor the technical project delivery and integrated quality review processes within the office, or within responsible offices, for all projects across all disciplines.

• Meet regularly with the Business Practice Leader (BPL) and provide information on project status and potential risk.

• Develop and implement with the region's Office Technical Leaders, Senior Project Architects and Project Engineering Leaders a strategy for continuous proactive Quality engagement.

• Meet regularly with project leadership in responsible offices to schedule and coordinate staffing and status for quality reviews for all disciplines and address ongoing challenges.

• Engage with the development of Project Risk Assessments and all phase updates. Support and help manage project risk mitigation strategies.

• Guide and assist teams in the development of Project Quality Plans and their updates to effectively manage project quality including phase milestone quality reviews and project pinups / technical charettes.

• Guide teams to implement the firm technical document standards and Construction Administration phase policies.

• Act as a proactive resource to project teams in their decision-making processes and provide support in the development of technically sound and innovative design solutions, focused on those projects at greatest risk. Engage members of the Technical Leadership Group as needed.

• Meet with project teams on a regular basis to monitor work in progress and ensure that the firm’s process standards and procedures are being implemented.

• Lead development of office quality plans that define a customized, effective quality strategy for the region and responsible offices.

• Attend, participate and engage in Technical Leader meetings held with the Technical Leadership Group. Contribute to ongoing planning with fellow Technical Leaders and the Technical Leadership Group to develop and improve quality resources.

• Monitor overall office metrics, including factors for risk, quality, sustainability, technology and construction, to identify and elevate near- and long-term concerns.

• Participate in the hiring process for new senior technical staff within the responsible offices and provide feedback on candidates.

• Strategically engage in project phase quality reviews, engaging and managing other project reviewers as needed. Act as lead quality reviewer for very large projects, organizing the efforts of others in reviewing specific scopes of work.

• Strategize to engage technical project leadership's proactive involvement in other projects to ensure that all projects have senior guidance and proactive mentoring.

• Establish strategies that drive the capture and reuse of institutional knowledge within the firm and share with the Technical Leadership Group.

• Write technical articles relating to technical quality subjects for internal and/or external publication within area of expertise.

• Evaluate and guide introduction of new building technologies, methods, and materials.

• Initiate and lead regular office forums to share technical insights and foster a culture of technical excellence. Lead and initiate ongoing mentoring and training to support continuous improvement.

• Meet established utilization target.

• May perform other duties as required.

HERE’S WHAT YOU’LL NEED

• Minimum Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field required.

• Minimum 18 years of related professional experience in Architecture and/or Engineering. Experience includes 5 years in increasingly responsible roles in construction documentation on institutional and/or commercial projects and at least 3 years in a responsible role in construction administration on large institutional and/or commercial projects.

• Current Architectural Registration or Professional Engineer license in the United States required.

• Must have extensive experience designing, documenting, coordinating and administering the construction of significant institutional and/or commercial projects. Expertise in institutional and/or commercial codes, standards and familiarity with proven solutions to address often wildly conflicting requirements between building authorities, client needs, construction technologies and insurance provisions is essential.

• Demonstrated focus on quality.

• LEED accreditation preferred.

• Experience leading all technical aspects with production teams on large, complex projects of more than $200M construction costs.

• Strong technical leadership with knowledge of building codes and requirements.

• Must have the ability to be client facing with strong verbal and written communication skills.

• Strong business acumen, technical knowledge, coordination skills and the ability to build a rapport with the project team is essential.

• Advanced understanding of REVIT and BIM workflows.

• Familiarity with Revit, Bluebeam, Microsoft Office, Teams, and construction management software.

The salary range for this position to be filled in the New York City office is $140,500 to $175,600 annually. This salary range is the range we believe is the anticipated range of possible base compensation at the timing of the posting. We may ultimately pay more or less than the anticipated salary range for the position. Employees may be eligible for discretionary bonuses. We offer a full benefit package including medical, dental and vision coverage and flexible spending account options and voluntary insurances. We have paid time off, flex-time schedules, remote work options and a 401k plan and employee perk programs. For a general overview of our benefits, please visit our careers page at https://www.cannondesign.com/careers/benefits. Actual compensation may vary from posting based on geographic location, work experience, education and/or skill level.

CannonDesign is a design practice where strategy, experience, architecture, engineering, and social impact converge. We don’t just dream up solutions — we create and bring them to life in ways to solve some of the biggest challenges facing our clients and the society. At the heart of everything we do is Living-Centered Design, a bold commitment to using our talents to not just improve the world but to truly reshape it for the better. It’s more than a philosophy — it’s who we are, and it drives us to make a meaningful, lasting difference every day.

We support equity, diversity, and inclusion efforts that benefit all employees through the leadership of our DEI Council, our Employee Resource Groups which are open to everyone, and other community initiatives.

It's not uncommon for scammers to create positions that look legitimate on other sites; never enter your information or apply for CannonDesign positions on any platform. jobs.title: Traffic Engineering Practice Lead - Tennessee
jobs.description:

This leadership position will be responsible for the strategic growth, technical excellence, operational performance, and business development of the firm's statewide traffic engineering practice.

The Practice Lead will oversee a team of traffic engineers delivering complex projects throughout Tennessee. The successful candidate will combine deep technical knowledge with strong client relationships, business development capabilities, and industry leadership.

This role is intended for a recognized transportation professional with demonstrated experience in traffic operations, traffic signal systems, multimodal transportation, transportation safety, intelligent transportation systems, and organizational leadership. Experience leading transportation programs for municipalities, state agencies, MPOs, or major consulting firms is highly desirable.

The ideal candidate will have a proven record of professional leadership within organizations such as the Institute of Transportation Engineers (ITE) and a strong reputation among transportation agencies and industry stakeholders.

AECOM offers experienced transportation leaders the opportunity to elevate their careers beyond project delivery and take ownership of a statewide practice with the support of a global organization. As Traffic Engineering Practice Lead, you will have the authority to shape business strategy, expand client relationships, mentor and build high-performing teams, and influence some of Tennessee's most significant transportation investments while leveraging AECOM's national network of technical experts, market leaders, and resources.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Practice Leadership

• Lead the statewide Traffic Engineering Practice for Tennessee.
• Execute annual strategic growth plans.
• Identify emerging market opportunities and transportation trends.

Business Development and Client Management

• Serve as Principal-in-Charge for key transportation clients.
• Develop and maintain executive-level relationships with TDOT, local governments, planning organizations, and private development clients.
• Lead proposal development and project pursuit strategies.
• Participate in client interviews and contract negotiations.
• Represent AECOM at conferences, professional meetings, and industry events.

Technical Leadership

• Provide technical oversight and quality control for:Traffic Engineering Studies and AssessmentsTraffic Signals and ITSTransportation SafetyMultimodal Transportation

Project Delivery Leadership

• Lead engineering efforts for traffic studies, reports, and operational analyses.
• Lead engineering efforts for traffic signal and ITS planning and design projects.
• Coordinate with roadway, bridge, drainage, environmental, and planning disciplines.
• Ensure projects are delivered on schedule, within budget, and at the highest level of quality.

Team Leadership and Staff Development

• Recruit, mentor, and develop transportation professionals.
• Build and maintain a high-performing statewide traffic engineering team.
• Conduct performance evaluations and professional development planning.
• Support professional licensure and technical certifications.
• Foster innovation and technical excellence throughout the practice.

Minimum:

• Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering or related field.
• 10 years of progressively responsible traffic engineering and transportation operations experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
• 5 years of project management and team leadership experience.
• Experience managing traffic engineering and ITS projects.

Preferred:

• Licensed Professional Engineer (P.E.).
• Professional Traffic Operations Engineer (PTOE) certification.
• Road Safety Professional (RSP) certification.
• IMSA Traffic Signal certifications.
• 15 years of traffic engineering and ITS experience.
• Experience with TDOT projects.
• Experience with municipal transportation programs.

• Relocation is an option for this position
• We are interested in every qualified candidate eligible to work in the United States. Sponsorship may be available for current visa holders in the United States
